providers.description: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd. (주식회사 곳간, branded KOKKAN / 도심창고 곳간) is a South Korean urban self-storage and logistics operator headquartered in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. It rents managed storage units in five sizes (S, M, L, XL, XXL, from 1.0m cubes up to 2.0 x 2.0 x 2.0m) across 22 branches in Seoul, Busan, Incheon, Gyeonggi and Chungbuk, serving households storing seasonal appliances, clothing, bedding and baby goods as well as businesses storing samples, inventory, documents and office equipment. Customers select a branch, choose a unit size, pay and manage their contract through the KOKKAN mobile apps for iOS and Android, with recurring monthly card billing through a Korean payment gateway, long-term and promotional discounting, an address-rental (주소지 임대) product, and an optional pickup service for moving stored goods. The company also runs a franchise and partnership program for operators who want to open a KOKKAN branch. It was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. As of this profile KokkanLogis publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or technical documentation — the product surface is a consumer website plus native mobile apps.

providers.name: Airspace Intelligence
providers.description: Air Space Intelligence (ASI) builds AI software for mission-critical, geospatial operations across aviation, defense, logistics, and energy. Its Prescience platform fuses data, models operational domains, runs predictive simulations, and optimizes complex operations in real time — spanning airline operations, air traffic management, global logistics, defense (space, air, land, sea), and energy grids. ASI holds an $875M FAA contract to help modernize the U.S. National Airspace System and works with partners including Alaska Airlines, National Grid, and the U.S. Air Force. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Solvo.ai
providers.description: Solvo.ai is a revenue-orchestration company building the decision layer for revenue management in container logistics. Its live pricing engine ingests market rates, capacity manifests, booking history, port congestion, customer behaviour and contract terms, then uses models trained on tens of millions of historical bookings to produce a ranked, capacity-aware rate recommendation per lane, equipment type and segment. Trade managers accept, adjust or override these recommendations on Solvo's Decision HUB, and every decision feeds back as training signal through a bidirectional integration with the carrier's commercial stack. Founded in 2021 and backed by Speedinvest, Solvo positions itself as the only proven, live pricing engine built specifically for container shipping, with one of the world's top carriers in production. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio company; Solvo currently publishes a marketing and insights site only, with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs or specifications.

providers.name: Trackonomy
providers.description: Trackonomy is a supply chain visibility company that digitizes real-world operations with barely-there smart label sensors. Its SmartTape and THL Tape products provide item-level tracking, monitoring location, temperature, humidity, and light in real time, while its platform connects, automates, controls, and remediates operations processes at global scale for logistics, industrial, utilities, healthcare, government, and airline customers. Trackonomy is backed by 8VC. It advertises a customizable RESTful API and webhook-based real-time data exchange for platform customers, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: CargoWise
providers.description: CargoWise is WiseTech Global's logistics execution platform - a single-database ERP for international freight forwarding, customs, warehousing, transport, and landside logistics. Its integration surface is delivered primarily through eAdaptor, which pairs a RESTful XML inbound service (push, query, add, and update records) with a SOAP-based outbound service (a webhook equivalent that emits messages on milestones). Payloads use CargoWise's Universal XML schemas - Universal Shipment (XUS), Universal Event (XUE), and Universal Transaction - or the legacy Native XML format. Newer REST integration (eAdaptor Next / xHub) adds OAuth 2.0 authorization-code access. The integration API is real but heavily gated - the eAdaptor Developers Guide and endpoint details are released only after a customer purchases the eAdaptor modules, and partner access runs through WiseTech accreditation and certification. Endpoints below are modeled from public developer references; the authoritative specification is not publicly published.

providers.name: Forward Air
providers.description: Forward Air is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Forward Air API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Heartland Express
providers.description: Heartland Express is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Heartland Express API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Jingle
providers.description: Jingle is a consumer marketplace mobile app for fast, direct local deliveries from mobile stores and services — "shops-on-wheels" — operating in the San Francisco Bay Area. Users sign up with a phone number (no password) and enable push notifications to be alerted when their favorite mobile vendors are nearby — artisanal food trucks, farmers'-market sellers, and one-click services such as bike repair, car wash, manicures, pedicures, and knife sharpening — then request a "jingle" to summon them. Deliveries are handled directly by the businesses themselves, cutting out delivery middlemen. Merchants use the app at their discretion to broadcast their presence to nearby neighborhoods, and residential complexes can partner to bring vendors on-site. Jingle is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its public consumer and merchant surface.

providers.name: Knight-Swift Transportation
providers.description: Knight-Swift Transportation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Knight-Swift Transportation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Open Port Technology
providers.description: Open Port Technology (OpenPort) is a pan-Asian logistics and supply chain technology company that digitizes trucking, freight, and supply chain operations across emerging markets through an open, neutral, AI-based platform. Headquartered in Karachi, Pakistan, its product suite spans transport management (OpenTM), a digital trucking marketplace (OpenMarket), customs clearance (OpenClear), warehouse picking operations (OpenPick), and FBR digital invoicing (Open Invoice). The company reports millions of completed shipments, 1,600+ transport partners, and integrations across 100+ ERP systems, offering ERP integration and custom API development to clients, though it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: TradeLink
providers.description: TradeLink is a Munich-based logistics SaaS company building the first collaboration platform for supply chain and inbound/outbound logistics. Its cloud software gives warehouses, suppliers, carriers, and dispatchers a shared system for time-slot (dock) booking, dock and yard management, load-carrier and empties management, driver check-in terminals, and analytics insights, replacing phone and email coordination with real-time, transparent workflows. TradeLink integrates with existing ERP and transport-management systems and serves production, retail, and contract-logistics companies across the DACH region and Europe, with customers including MAN, SPAR, Liebherr, and Emons. It is backed by Insight Partners and Point Nine.

providers.name: Operation Support Equipment
providers.description: API for managing and accessing operation support equipment data, inventory, maintenance records, and deployment information for operational logistics and equipment lifecycle management.

providers.name: RightHand Robotics
providers.description: RightHand Robotics builds autonomous piece-picking robotic systems for order fulfillment. Its RightPick platform combines computer vision, machine learning, and adaptive grasping hardware to pick and place millions of SKUs at cycle times as fast as three seconds across e-commerce, pharmaceutical, apparel, health & beauty, and grocery operations. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and SoftBank Vision Fund. RightHand Robotics does not publish a public web API; integration, deployment, and operator documentation is provided to authorized customers and partners through a login-gated partner portal (rhrdocs.com). The public GitHub organization hosts open-source ROS packages and C control libraries for the earlier ReFlex robotic hand hardware rather than web-API client SDKs.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: Mubit
providers.description: Mubit is a temporary storage and logistics service based in Guadalajara, Mexico, offering on-demand collection, climate-controlled warehousing, digital photo inventory, and delivery for both individuals and businesses. Customers pay only for the space they use, with free pickup and drop-off, optional professional packing, and 24/7 CCTV-monitored facilities across three warehouses (Colli, Tijera, and Casuarina). Backed by 500 Global and Techstars, the company reports 4,000+ customers and a 4.9-star Google rating, and operates a mobile/web customer portal at clientes.mubit.co for scheduling pickups and deliveries and viewing stored items. Mubit publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Plus One Robotics
providers.description: Plus One Robotics is a San Antonio, Texas warehouse-automation company founded in 2016 by Erik Nieves and Shaun Edwards that builds AI-powered computer-vision software and robotic work cells for parcel handling, depalletizing, palletizing and induction. Its PickOne perception system tells a robot arm how to grasp each item and verifies placement, while Yonder provides supervised autonomy — remote human "Crew Chiefs" who take over when the robot hits an exception. Packaged work cells DepalOne and InductOne wrap that stack in deployable hardware. The company reports more than 1.5 billion lifetime picks across robots fielded in 15 countries, with additional offices in Eindhoven (Netherlands) and Boulder, Colorado. Plus One Robotics publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; product integration is handled through its partner channel and a login-gated partner portal.

providers.name: Route
providers.description: Route is a post-purchase platform for e-commerce brands that helps merchants own the customer experience after checkout. Its core products are package protection (shipping insurance covering lost, stolen, or damaged orders), AI-driven returns that reduce refunds and returns fraud, and real-time order and package tracking for shoppers. Route serves both merchants and their customers through storefront widgets, a mobile app, and a developer API documented on Stoplight. The company is backed by Craft Ventures.

providers.name: Saia Inc
providers.description: Saia Inc is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Saia Inc API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Starship Technologies
providers.description: Starship Technologies is an autonomous last-mile delivery company that operates a global fleet of self-driving, sidewalk-going delivery robots. Founded in 2014 by Skype co-founders Ahti Heinla and Janus Friis, the company runs commercial robot delivery on university campuses, in residential neighborhoods, on industrial sites and for grocery and restaurant partners across the United States, the United Kingdom, Estonia, Finland, Germany and Denmark, and has completed more than 10 million autonomous deliveries. Its commercial product, Delivery by Starship, is a delivery-as-a-service offering that partners integrate into their own ordering apps: Starship states that its APIs let a partner create delivery jobs, load robots, obtain status updates and handle delivery cancellations, backed by a developer toolkit, documentation, ready-made components and support. That developer surface is not published to the open web — Starship provides it to partners after a commercial conversation via business@starship.co, so no public specification, reference or portal exists to profile.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Booster Fuels
providers.description: Booster (Booster Fuels, Inc.) is a mobile energy delivery company that brings gasoline, diesel, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and renewable fuel alternatives directly to vehicles, fleets, and on-site fuel tanks using a fleet of Smart Tankers, removing the need for drivers to visit gas stations. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile is a company/lead entry in the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Reibus
providers.description: Reibus is a technology-enabled B2B platform for the industrial metals industry, originally a digital marketplace for buying and selling steel and other metals and now focused on open-deck freight logistics for shipping steel and industrial metals. Operating as Reibus Logistics, the company connects shippers with a vast network of international and domestic carriers across flatbed, dry van, and drayage modes, offering instant quoting, shipment visibility, and cross-border logistics in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Founded by CEO John Blount, Reibus operates in 7 countries, does business in 25+ countries, and is backed by Canaan Partners, Initialized Capital, and the SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: SVT Robotics
providers.description: SVT Robotics builds the SOFTBOT Platform, a software integration and orchestration foundation for warehouse automation and the supply chain. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia, the company lets enterprises connect industrial systems, robotics, AMRs, and warehouse management software through standardized, prebuilt SOFTBOT Connectors — reducing integration complexity and enabling real-time visibility, faster automation deployments, and a resilient data backbone for automation and AI. Customers include DHL Supply Chain, Barrett Distribution Centers, and the Hagen Group. The provider operates a developer documentation hub for the SOFTBOT integration API (docs.svtrobotics.com, currently password-protected) and a public status page; no public OpenAPI, SDK, or open API surface was discoverable at enrichment time.

providers.name: Lyric
providers.description: Lyric is an AI-powered supply chain software company, founded in 2022 and backed by Insight Partners. Its Lyric Studio platform lets enterprises model, plan, and optimize their supply chains across four composable layers — Data (enterprise-grade data management and integrations), Algorithms (advanced supply chain science), Workflows (flexible, composable processes), and Models & Apps (ready-to-use applications). The platform spans network modeling, transportation optimization, inventory management, forecasting, routing, and scheduling. Lyric does not publish a public developer API surface; its product documentation at docs.lyric.tech is gated behind a Lyric Studio login. It does operate a public SafeBase security and trust portal documenting SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR, CCPA, CPRA, and CSA STAR Level 1 posture plus a responsible disclosure program.

providers.name: Pharmapacks
providers.description: Pharmapacks was a New York-based e-commerce marketplace seller and third-party logistics operator, founded in 2010 in Long Island City, that grew into one of the largest independent sellers of health, beauty and personal-care goods on Amazon, eBay and Walmart Marketplace. The company rebranded as Packable Holdings LLC in 2021, agreed a SPAC merger with Highland Transcend Partners I Corp. that was abandoned in March 2022, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 2022-08-28 before ceasing operations and liquidating substantially all of its assets. Its differentiator was an internal "Master Brain" marketplace-listing, repricing and fulfillment platform, but that technology was operated as an internal system and was never published as a public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable contract has ever been found on any host the company controlled. The pharmapacks.com domain is today a GoDaddy parking lander. A successor brand operating as Packable at packable.com, led by Pharmapacks/Packable co-founder Jonathan Webb, sells fulfillment, logistics and digital-enablement services and likewise publishes no public API.

providers.name: Avathon
providers.description: Avathon — formerly SparkCognition, rebranded in November 2024 — is an industrial AI company whose Industrial AI Platform combines a data platform, industrial digital twin, AI modeling and application development layers to bring predictive maintenance, asset performance management, visual intelligence and autonomy to physical operations. Its solutions span renewables, oil and gas, power and utilities, manufacturing, mining, aerospace and defense, maritime, rail, aviation, logistics, warehousing and retail, with named offerings including Asset Performance Management, Visual AI / Visual Intelligence, Autonomy for Health, Safety and Environment, the Digital Maintenance Advisor and the Multidomain Awareness Advisor. The platform is sold and delivered as an enterprise engagement — marketing material references an application development SDK and APIs, but no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published; the only documentation surface, support.avathon.com/help, redirects to a HubSpot member login. Avathon is backed by investors including Temasek, Verizon Ventures and Boeing, and is headquartered in Silicon Valley after relocating from Austin, Texas.

providers.name: Cycle
providers.description: CYCLE (operated by CM Invest B.V., Amsterdam) is a European electric-mobility subscription service that provides e-bikes and cargo bikes to professional delivery riders, couriers, and businesses. Its all-inclusive monthly subscriptions bundle maintenance, on-site repairs, bike swaps, GPS tracking, theft protection, and remote motor control across 100+ cities in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Belgium, Poland, Italy, and the UK. CYCLE was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the provider publishes a consumer/business marketing and operations site but exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Forum Mobility
providers.description: Forum Mobility develops, owns, and operates zero-emission heavy-duty trucking infrastructure, bundling electric Class 8 truck leases with charging subscriptions for a single monthly price so freight carriers of every size can electrify without upfront capital. The company builds and runs a network of charging depots — anchored by its flagship FM Harbor site at the Port of Long Beach (44 ports, 360KW fast chargers, 9MW capacity) — with additional depots in development across California and Nevada. Forum Mobility was surfaced as a portfolio company of obvious-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a physical-infrastructure operator with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Geek+
providers.description: Geek+ (Geekplus, HKEX: 2590) is a global leader in AI-driven autonomous mobile robot (AMR) solutions for warehouse and logistics automation. Founded in 2015, it delivers end-to-end smart-warehouse systems spanning shelf-to-person (PopPick), tote-to-person (RoboShuttle), pallet-to-person (Skycube) storage and retrieval, robot-arm picking, sorting, and intralogistics transport. Its All-in-One Software Suite (Robot Management System, Warehouse Execution System, Intelligent Warehouse Management System, data and simulation platforms) exposes open REST APIs and SDKs so customers and partners can integrate robot fleets with major WMS, ERP, and MES platforms including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Manhattan Associates, and Blue Yonder. Geek+ serves 3PL, retail, e-commerce, apparel, grocery, healthcare and pharma, manufacturing, automotive, electronics, and cold-chain logistics across 40+ countries, with 950+ deployed warehouses. In 2025 it became the world's first publicly listed AMR warehouse robotics company on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

providers.name: iMile
providers.description: iMile is a technology-driven last-mile delivery and e-commerce logistics company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Led by founder and CEO Rita Huang, iMile provides express parcel delivery, cash-on-delivery (COD), domestic and international express, dropshipping, order fulfillment, warehousing, storage, and reverse logistics / return management across more than 30 countries spanning the Middle East, China, Latin America, Africa, Europe, and Australia. The company operates its own routing, tracking, and delivery technology and employs over 20,000 people. iMile assigns each shipment a 13-digit tracking number; parcel tracking is available on imile.com and through major third-party tracking aggregators. iMile does not currently publish a first-party public developer API or open platform, so this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Metro Africa Xpress
providers.description: Metro Africa Xpress (MAX), operating as maxdrive.ai, is a Nigerian technology-driven mobility company on a mission to make transportation safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable across Africa. MAX finances and deploys vehicles — including electric two- and three-wheelers — to a vetted network of driver-partners ("champions"), and runs a drivers services platform, electric-vehicle assembly and charging infrastructure, enterprise last-mile logistics, and mobility gov-tech solutions. Emerging from the MIT and Techstars ecosystem, MAX is backed by Novastar Ventures, Goodwell, Shell Foundation, Breakthrough Energy, Capria and Yamaha, and operates across Nigeria, Cameroon and other West African markets. The company publishes a marketing and corporate website only; no public developer program, API, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Rapido
providers.description: Rapido is an Indian on-demand urban mobility platform that connects riders with independent driver-partners (called "Captains") for bike taxis, auto rickshaws, and cabs through its consumer and Captain mobile apps. Founded in Bengaluru and backed by Accel, Rapido operates across hundreds of Indian cities and has expanded into parcel delivery and corporate mobility. As of this enrichment pass Rapido exposes only a consumer-facing web and app surface — no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification was found. This profile captures the company identity, its published policy and content pages, and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Rebel Foods
providers.description: Rebel Foods is an Indian cloud-kitchen operator, headquartered in Mumbai, that describes itself as the world's largest chain of internet restaurants. It runs a portfolio of delivery-first food brands — Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, Oven Story, Firangi Bake, The Good Bowl, Sweet Truth, Mandarin Oak, The Biryani Life and Lunch Box — out of a shared network of cloud kitchens, and consolidates them for consumers in the EatSure ordering app. Its internal technology platform, the Rebel Operating System, handles kitchen workflow, inventory, demand forecasting, order routing and logistics, and is offered to third-party restaurant chains through the Rebel Launcher partner programme. That platform is a commercial partnership, not a self-serve developer product: as of this profile Rebel Foods publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Robust.AI
providers.description: Robust.AI is a robotics company building Carter, an AI-powered collaborative mobile robot for warehouse fulfillment and manufacturing environments. Founded by Rodney Brooks (co-founder of iRobot and Rethink Robotics) and colleagues, the company designs human-centered autonomous material-handling robots that work alongside people with minimal infrastructure change, no capital expenditure, and rapid ROI. Robust.AI is backed by Playground Global and was recognized among Fast Company's World's Most Innovative Companies of 2026. This is a physical-robotics company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or GitHub surface.

providers.name: Saucey
providers.description: Saucey is an on-demand alcohol delivery service that brings beer, wine, and spirits from local retailers to customers' doors, often in under an hour, across a growing list of US markets. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Los Angeles, the company operates consumer iOS, Android, and web ordering experiences, a Saucey Club membership offering free delivery and perks, and a retailer/brand partnership program. Saucey is backed by 500 Global and Bullpen Capital. This profile tracks Saucey in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Saucey publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Shopeando
providers.description: Shopeando is a Mexican technology and logistics startup that manages the full international shipping process, enabling businesses and individuals to import and export merchandise between China, Europe, the United States and Mexico. Through its platform it coordinates cross-border logistics, customs handling and last-mile delivery, and provides dedicated import, export and e-commerce fulfillment services for online stores. Shopeando is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Swift Transportation
providers.description: Swift Transportation, now operating as Knight-Swift Transportation Holdings (KNX), is the largest full truckload motor carrier in North America. The company provides truckload, LTL, logistics, and intermodal transportation services across the US, Mexico, and Canada. Technology integration is primarily through EDI for freight tendering, shipment status, and invoicing workflows with trading partners and shippers.

providers.name: Viewlocity
providers.description: Viewlocity Technologies Pty Ltd is a supply chain management software company that provides supply chain visibility, control tower, and execution solutions for global manufacturers, distributors, and logistics providers. Its solution set spans supply chain design, inventory and asset management, supply chain management, logistics and transportation, planning and production, order lifecycle management, and supplier management, delivered as SaaS and managed services to industries including aerospace and defense, automotive and industrial, consumer goods, high tech and electronics, manufacturing, retail, and third-party logistics. Viewlocity publishes a corporate marketing and resource website but does not expose a public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Fleetline
providers.description: Fleetline is an all-in-one AI dispatch and fleet-optimization platform for trucking fleets. Its AI-based dispatch engine ingests load, driver, and ELD data, simulates billions of scenarios, and recommends the best assignment plan so operators maximize revenue, productivity, and fleet utilization. The platform aggregates major load boards into a unified workspace, identifies schedule gaps and fills them with spot loads, composes complex trips with tradeoff analysis, forecasts delays, breakdowns, and HOS violations, and includes an AI assistant trained on fleet history and TMS data. Fleetline is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; it exposes a marketing site, a customer login/auth portal, and an internal API host, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Good Eggs
providers.description: Good Eggs is an online grocery marketplace founded in 2011 that delivers "absurdly fresh" groceries, meal kits, and locally sourced food to homes across the West Coast of the United States, primarily the San Francisco Bay Area and Southern California. The company curates a marketplace of over 6,000 items from local farms, ranches, fisheries, and independent food makers, and operates its own fulfillment and same-day/next-day delivery logistics. Good Eggs is a consumer-facing e-commerce and delivery business; it maintains a verified public GitHub organization for its engineering open-source and internal tooling but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (GV, Index Ventures, Obvious Ventures) and enriched with the company's real public web properties.

providers.name: Oxa
providers.description: Oxa (formerly Oxbotica, rebranded in 2023) is a British autonomous vehicle software company founded in 2014 in Oxford, England by Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner. Oxa builds what it calls Universal Autonomy — self-driving software configurable for almost any vehicle in almost any environment — and sells it as Industrial Mobility Automation for ports, airports, manufacturing yards, solar farms and shuttle networks. Its product line is Oxa Driver (the autonomy stack), Oxa Foundry (a generative-AI training and assurance toolchain, previously marketed as Oxa MetaDriver), Reference Autonomy Designs (modular hardware integration blueprints), and Oxa Hub (a cloud fleet-management suite covering remote assist, task design, workspace mapping, digital twins and in-use monitoring). Oxa Hub is described on the marketing site as offering "an API for optional integration with existing logistics systems", but Oxa publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable specification on any public host. The company raised a $115M Series C in 2023 with participation from Google, and works with Ocado Group, ZF and bp.

providers.name: Canadian National Railway
providers.description: Canadian National Railway (CN) is the largest railway network in Canada and one of the largest in North America spanning over 20,000 route miles. CN transports goods across an integrated network linking the Atlantic and Pacific coasts with the Gulf of Mexico. CN offers shipper APIs, EDI integration, the eBusiness portal, and the CN ONE mobile app for shipment tracking, ordering, billing, and rate management.

providers.name: Stack AV
providers.description: Stack AV is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania autonomous-vehicle company founded in 2023 by Bryan Salesky (CEO), Peter Rander (President) and Brett Browning (CTO) — the leadership team behind Argo AI — and backed by SoftBank Group. The company develops AI-driven autonomy software and hardware for Class 8 commercial freight trucking, targeting driver shortages, vehicle uptime, safety, operating cost and emissions, and in May 2026 unveiled its first autonomous truck built in collaboration with PACCAR and Peterbilt Motors. Stack AV runs a public open-source engineering organization at github.com/stackav-oss (dltype, conch Triton kernels, clockwork, scene-tokens, push-guard, ai-workloads). It publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract as of August 2026 — the product is an autonomous freight service, not a developer platform.

providers.name: Guazi
providers.description: Guazi is a China-based used-car export, auction, and trading platform founded in 2015 and headquartered in Beijing. It connects international dealers and buyers with used vehicles sourced across China, offering sealed-bid online auctions, Buy It Now direct sales, a 200-plus-point vehicle inspection process, direct sourcing on request, and global logistics shipping to more than 50 countries via container and Ro-Ro. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, HongShan (Sequoia China), and Tencent, Guazi handles over 200,000 vehicles annually. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence; no public developer program, API, or SDK has been found.

providers.name: PitPro Automation
providers.description: PitPro Automation is a fleet-maintenance technology company building automated tire-service systems that perform full tire changes and rotations on commercial fleet vehicles in under fifteen minutes. Targeting Class 2 and smaller vehicles, the company serves last-mile delivery, rideshare, utility, telecom, moving, and government fleets with in-bay automation, 24/7 monitoring, and field support. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, PitPro is a hardware-and-software provider focused on reducing fleet downtime; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Sensefinity
providers.description: Sensefinity is a supply-chain IoT company ("The IoT Transformation Company") delivering real-time tracking, monitoring, and analytics for global cargo and logistics operations. Its platform combines GPS/NB-IoT tracking devices for maritime containers, pallets, and vehicles with temperature and condition (cold-chain) sensors, indoor location tracking, a cloud analytics and machine learning layer, and digital product passport / blockchain integrations. The operational platform is delivered as a hosted web application (uiadmin.sensefinity.com) and mobile asset-management apps, serving enterprise customers across food, pharma, automotive, and manufacturing supply chains. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published as of this profile; a private API host (api.sensefinity.com) backs the platform.

providers.name: Shippingbo
providers.description: Shippingbo is a Toulouse, France-based e-commerce logistics SaaS founded in 2016 by Marc Hericher and Romain Parent. The platform unifies an Order Management System (OMS), Warehouse Management System (WMS), and Transport Management System (TMS) behind a single REST API so that merchants, DNVBs, 3PLs, wholesalers, manufacturers, and marketplaces can centralize multi-channel orders, pilot warehouse picking and packing, and execute multi-carrier shipments from one back office. Shippingbo claims 5,000+ active users, 80 million orders, and EUR 5 billion in merchandise handled in 2024, with 2,500+ warehouses equipped across France and Europe. The Shippingbo Developer Portal (powered by Stoplight) exposes a public REST/JSON API covering orders, products, stocks, shipments, customers, pickings, and source connectors, secured by OAuth 2.0 through the oauth.shippingbo.com authorization server. Shippingbo additionally offers a dedicated TMS API for multi-carrier label generation and a webhook channel for order state changes, stock changes, and shipment events. Reported developer-facing scale includes 500+ developers, 10+ million orders processed through the APIs, 500+ million webhook deliveries, and 40+ pre-integrated carriers. Shippingbo is a French Tech company backed by IRDI Capital Investissement and GSO Innovation.

providers.name: Snowman
providers.description: Snowman Logistics is an Indian integrated cold-chain and temperature-controlled logistics company headquartered in Bengaluru, providing refrigerated (frozen and chilled) warehousing, cold storage, and distribution services across India. It serves frozen and chilled foods, dairy, seafood, quick-service restaurants, pharmaceuticals, and other perishables through a national network of temperature-controlled warehouses and a refrigerated transportation fleet. The company is publicly listed on Indian exchanges and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the enrichment pass confirmed the company publishes a marketing/corporate website (snowman.in) but exposes no public developer, API, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Olist
providers.description: Olist is a Brazilian commerce technology company headquartered in Curitiba, Paraná, offering an integrated ecosystem of solutions that automate business management for online sellers. Its products include an ERP for inventory, invoicing and order automation, a multi-marketplace Integration Hub (Mercado Livre, TikTok Shop and others), a POS for physical stores, a digital account with Pix payments, shipping and fulfillment (Envios), and storefront creation. Olist exposes robust partner APIs through its Technology Partner program ("Parceiro Tecnológico"), where approved developers receive test credentials and Swagger documentation to build and homologate integrations reaching 60,000+ merchants. The public API surface is gated behind partner registration; no open developer portal or OpenAPI specification is published.

providers.name: Reibus International
providers.description: Reibus International is an Atlanta, Georgia headquartered technology company operating a digital marketplace and open-deck freight logistics platform for the industrial metals industry. Reibus connects buyers and sellers of steel and other industrial metals with a curated network of international and domestic carriers, offering instant freight quotes, automated carrier assignment, and real-time shipment visibility tracking. The Reibus Logistics platform specializes in flatbed, dry van, and dray transportation across the contiguous United States, Canada, and Mexico, plus specialized services including oversized loads, team drivers, expedited shipping, cross-border logistics, high-value freight, and warehousing. Founded by CEO John Blount, Reibus operates across seven countries with business relationships spanning more than 25 nations and is backed by Battery Ventures. Reibus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; customer-facing tools (instant quote, shipment visibility dashboard) are delivered through the app.reibus.com web application.

providers.name: Flyzipline
providers.description: Flyzipline (Zipline International Inc., flyzipline.com / zipline.com) designs, manufactures, and operates autonomous delivery drones for food, groceries, and medicine. Its instant logistics platform flies vital shipments — blood products, vaccines, pharmaceuticals, prepared meals, and retail goods — on direct aerial routes at up to 70 mph, with temperature-controlled pods and real-time tracking. Zipline operates distribution centers across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan, partnering with health systems, retailers (Walmart, Chipotle), and restaurant technology providers (Olo) that submit delivery requests through Zipline's ordering system or software integrations. As of early 2026 the fleet has completed more than two million commercial deliveries across 120+ million autonomous miles. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-adjacent portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Zipline publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time — partner integrations are bespoke.

providers.name: VOO (now SideUp)
providers.description: VOO was an Egyptian logistics marketplace that rebranded as SideUp in December 2022, relocating its headquarters to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. SideUp is a fully integrated courier marketplace that lets e-commerce businesses ship locally and globally from one dashboard, connecting merchants with multiple courier services alongside payment gateways, shipping API integration, warehousing, and fulfillment, with plugins for Shopify, Salla, and OpenCart. Backed by 500 Global, Launch Africa VC, Riyadh Angels, and Alex Angels ($1.2M seed). No public developer portal or API documentation is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: Watsco
providers.description: Watsco, Inc. is the world's largest distributor of air conditioning, heating, and refrigeration (HVAC/R) equipment and related products. Operating through subsidiaries including Carrier Enterprise, Baker Distributing, Gemaire Distributors, and East Coast Metal Distributors, Watsco serves contractors and dealers across more than 670 locations in the US, Canada, Mexico, and the Caribbean. The company has undergone significant digital transformation, running a unified B2B e-commerce platform powered by Magento Commerce and a centralized PIM system covering approximately 900,000 SKUs.

providers.name: Blau Corp
providers.description: Blau (Blau Corp) is a waste-management operating system for haulers (gestores), final-destination facilities, and government regulators across Mexico, Colombia, and Spain. The SaaS platform delivers AI-assisted route optimization, route-level profitability analysis, automated RP and RPBI hazardous- and biological-infectious-waste manifests, online collection booking, and end-to-end traceability, plus the Blau Driver mobile app for field crews. Founded in Guadalajara, Mexico in 2021 and backed by 500 Global (LatAm B17 batch), Blau integrates with SAT/CFDI, SEMARNAT, SAP/ERP, QuickBooks, WhatsApp, fleet GPS, and Power BI. Blau does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Vekia
providers.description: Vekia is a French supply-chain software vendor founded in 2008 in Lille by Manuel Davy (Vekia SAS, 143 rue d'Athènes, 59800 Lille, RCS Lille Métropole 503 225 716). Its platform, Vekia Engine, applies probabilistic artificial intelligence and machine learning to demand and stock forecasting, then generates optimised purchase-order proposals that are pushed back into the customer's existing ERP rather than replacing it, alongside shortage-risk alerting and a logistics control tower. Vekia Disrupt covers disruption and shortage management. The platform is hosted on Microsoft Azure in Europe and marketed to retail and specialised distribution, e-commerce, industry, energy and telecom, with published case studies at ENGIE, Mr Bricolage and Okaïdi. Vekia publishes no public API, no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract; ERP, WMS and TMS integration is delivered as a project by Vekia rather than through a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: WESCO International
providers.description: WESCO International is a Fortune 500 leading provider of business-to-business distribution, logistics services, and supply chain solutions for electrical, industrial, communications, and utility customers worldwide. WESCO serves over 150,000 customers through a network of branches and distribution centers and provides comprehensive digital integration capabilities including EDI, punchout, cXML, and API connectivity for procurement automation.

providers.name: Dexory
providers.description: Dexory is a UK-based warehouse intelligence and robotics company whose DexoryView platform pairs fleets of autonomous mobile scanning robots with physical AI to deliver real-time "ground truth" visibility across warehouses and distribution centers. The robots autonomously scan more than 10,000 pallet locations per hour and up to 18 meters of racking height, building a live digital twin that feeds AI-driven analytics for inventory accuracy, space and slotting optimization, damage/compliance detection, and operational performance. DexoryView is organized into modules (Integrity for stock accuracy and automated cycle counts, Optimise for space and productivity analytics, and Adapt for real-time operational response) and connects into existing warehouse and ERP systems such as SAP EWM, Manhattan, Blue Yonder, and Körber through pre-built connectors. Dexory serves 3PL logistics, manufacturing, food & beverage, retail, pharma, and air cargo operators. Added to the API Evangelist network from Atomico's portfolio and enriched via the pipeline; Dexory does not currently publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Gather AI
providers.description: Gather AI is a Physical AI platform for logistics that gives warehouses dock-to-dock inventory visibility. Cameras mounted on autonomous drones and forklifts capture inventory, and computer vision extracts structured data (LPNs, UPCs, lot codes, and free text) from the imagery. Its Sage AI engine analyzes operations and surfaces prioritized actions before each shift, while automated Workflows route tasks to the right personnel across integrated systems. The plug-and-play solution deploys in hours alongside existing warehouse management systems, serving manufacturing, healthcare, food & beverage, retail, and 3PL operations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: Shiplyst
providers.description: Shiplyst is an India-based ocean freight procurement marketplace and supply-chain technology platform that lets exporters and importers search and compare container shipping rates from 50+ ocean carriers in real time, generate instant quotes, book containers with transparent pricing, and track cargo from pickup to delivery. The platform automates Bill of Lading and invoice generation and offers real-time tracking with exception alerts across its web and mobile apps. Shiplyst is backed by 500 Global. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Swiggy
providers.description: Swiggy is an Indian hyperlocal on-demand commerce and food-delivery platform founded in 2014 and headquartered in Bengaluru. Through a single consumer app it connects users with restaurant and merchant partners for food delivery, Swiggy Instamart (quick grocery and essentials commerce), Swiggy Genie (pick-up and drop errands), Swiggy Dineout (restaurant reservations and dining), and the Swiggy One membership program, operating across hundreds of cities in India with a large network of restaurant and delivery partners. Swiggy is a publicly listed company backed by Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners, Norwest Venture Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund. It exposes a login-gated merchant partner portal but does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Agro Club
providers.description: Agro.Club is a US-based agtech company operating a digital grain trading and crop marketing marketplace that connects farmers with grain buyers. The platform offers competitive bids for corn, wheat, soybeans and other grains, along with logistics (truck and rail transportation), quality control, financing, and market insights. Farmers can transact through cash, FOB or delivered, and basis contracts, plus a Firm Offer price-target monitoring service. Agro.Club serves tens of thousands of farmers and grain companies across the largest agricultural hubs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. Agro.Club does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation; its api.agro.club host is a private backend that serves the company's own applications.

providers.name: Bloom & Wild
providers.description: Bloom & Wild is a British direct-to-consumer online florist and gifting brand founded in 2013 by Aron Gelbard and Ben Stanway, best known for pioneering letterbox flowers — bouquets packed flat so they fit through a UK letterbox — alongside hand-tied bouquets, plants, gift sets, gift cards and recurring flower subscriptions. Bloom & Wild Group trades as Bloom & Wild in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany and Austria, and operates the sister brands bloomon (Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark) and Bergamotte (France) on separate storefronts. The group is a certified B Corp and runs its own commerce platform — a Ruby on Rails backend fronted by Kong, an Angular multi-brand web app and native iOS and Android clients, on AWS and GCP. Bloom & Wild publishes NO public developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable API description, and no partner or corporate-gifting API: business and bulk gifting is transacted through a contact form, an account manager and invoicing, not through a programmatic surface. The application backends at api.bloomandwild.com and capi.bloomandwild.com are live but private to the brand's own clients and undocumented. What the group does publish for machines is narrow but real: an llms.txt on the UK and German storefronts that routes assistants to the correct market by delivery destination and even ships an optional agent widget specification, and an RFC 9116 security.txt served across every group storefront.

providers.name: Carnot Fleet
providers.description: Carnot Fleet (Carnotfleet) is a Seoul-based cold-chain technology company that converts non-refrigerated vehicles into temperature-controlled units in under 30 minutes using modular insulation panels and proprietary solid-state thermoelectric heat pumps, spanning frozen, chilled, and ambient ranges with humidity control. Its Adaptive Thermal Control System (ATCS) is an AI-based autonomous control platform delivering cloud-connected temperature monitoring at 10-second intervals. Carnot Fleet surfaces its capabilities through the CF Mobile Application, the CF Portal, and CF APIs that let customers integrate the ATCS into existing logistics solutions to detect, analyze, prevent, and discover cold-chain data points and reduce post-harvest to pre-retail loss across the supply chain.

providers.name: blueflite
providers.description: blueflite is a Techstars-backed unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) company that designs and manufactures autonomous cargo and delivery drones built on its SLATE platform for all-weather, time-sensitive logistics. Its aircraft target last-mile shipping and medical or life-saving delivery (such as defibrillators and emergency supplies), and the company complements the hardware with blueDelivery (a consumer ordering app), blueDigital (a cloud productivity tool), and blueControl, alongside drone consulting, engineering, and project services. blueflite is on the FAA Section 44807 approved UAS list and holds FCC conditional approval, and was founded by Frank Noppel and James McClearen. No public developer or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: MedArrive
providers.description: MedArrive is a healthcare technology company that provides a logistics and workforce platform for in-home care delivery. Its software gives health systems and in-home care providers smart scheduling, real-time provider routing, automated re-routing and patient reminders, and a live command-center dashboard for tracking every provider and visit, alongside a provider mobile app for field teams. The HIPAA-compliant platform is designed to reduce windshield time, cut scheduling effort, and increase daily visit capacity so care teams spend more time with patients and less on logistics. MedArrive is backed by Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Agility Robotics
providers.description: Agility Robotics is a Salem, Oregon humanoid robotics company building industrial bipedal robots for warehouse and factory automation. Founded in 2015 as a spin-out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Laboratory, its flagship product is Digit — described as the first humanoid robot in commercial production deployment — and Arc, the cloud-based automation platform that operates Digit fleets, provides real-time visibility, manages task assignments, and connects Digit to existing warehouse automation including AMRs, WMS, and WES systems. Digit has commercial deployments and pilots with Amazon, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre, with an expanded NVIDIA partnership for foundation-model and simulation tooling. Agility operates RoboFab, a humanoid robot factory in Salem, OR with capacity to produce 10,000 robots annually. Digit has surpassed 100,000 totes moved in commercial deployment at a single Georgia facility. Agility Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Digit or Arc; integration is performed by Agility's solutions team and partners through a gated low-level JSON-over-WebSocket API and pysdk delivered with the robot. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (JFrog, Bazel, Fluent Bit, Kubernetes Cluster API) plus an archived documentation repo for the earlier Cassie research platform.

providers.name: Cargo X
providers.description: Cargo X (CargoX) is a Sao Paulo based Brazilian logistics technology and fintech company, founded in 2013, that operates one of Brazil's largest digital freight marketplaces - matching shippers (embarcadores) with carriers (transportadoras) and independent truck drivers. Beyond freight brokerage the platform provides dedicated freight desk operations, driver qualification and real-time cargo monitoring, automated issuance of Brazilian transport tax documents (CT-e and MDF-e), cargo insurance, receivables financing and working-capital credit for carriers, and green-freight / ESG programs that reduce empty return trips. The company reached unicorn status with a USD 200M Series F in October 2021 co-led by Tencent and SoftBank, with Valor Capital Group, Lightrock and Oikos participating.

providers.name: Dronamics
providers.description: Dronamics is a European deep-tech company that designs, builds, and operates autonomous long-range cargo drones for middle-mile logistics. Its flagship aircraft, The Black Swan, is a remotely piloted UAV that carries up to 350 kg (770 lb) of cargo over distances up to 2,500 km (1,550 mi), enabling same-day, cross-border, point-to-point deliveries that are faster, cheaper, and lower in CO2 emissions than traditional air freight. Founded in 2014 in Sofia, Bulgaria by brothers Svilen and Konstantin Rangelov and operating as Dronamics Group Limited, the company is building the world's first cargo drone airline, operating a proprietary drone fleet from a network of low-cost droneports. The public dronamics.com marketing site is built on Wix and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access; Dronamics does not publish a developer-facing logistics API, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Werner Enterprises
providers.description: Werner Enterprises is a leading transportation and logistics company providing truckload transportation services, logistics solutions, and supply chain management throughout North America. Founded in 1956 and headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, Werner operates one of the largest fleets in the United States and offers freight brokerage, dedicated carriage, intermodal, and final-mile delivery services through its Werner Bridge℠ digital freight platform.

providers.name: DP World
providers.description: DP World is an Emirati global logistics company that specializes in port operations, maritime services, and supply chain solutions. It manages and operates marine and inland terminals across more than 40 countries and operates a portfolio of digital platforms - including the CARGOES suite (Flow, Runner, TOS+, PCS, Customs), Searates, and the Digital Freight Alliance - that expose APIs and integrations for shipment visibility, freight pricing, terminal operations, and trade workflows.

providers.name: jokr
providers.description: JOKR is an instant grocery and convenience delivery company headquartered in Luxembourg (JOKR S.a.r.L) that operates an online supermarket delivering fresh products and local brands to consumers within minutes or on a scheduled window through its mobile app. The service offers more than 10,000 products with AI-powered personalized recommendations and competitive supermarket pricing, and reports roughly 3 million app downloads and 5 million users. In Brazil it operates under the DAKI brand (soudaki.com), the leading online supermarket in cities including Sao Paulo and Belo Horizonte. JOKR is a consumer-facing quick-commerce business with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain posture in the API Evangelist network. Backed by Balderton Capital, GGV Capital, and HV Capital.

providers.name: Mytra
providers.description: Mytra, Inc. is a Brisbane, California robotics company founded in 2022 by former Tesla robotics lead Chris Walti, building what it calls software-defined warehousing: a three-part system of low-profile MytraBots that travel in X, Y and Z through a modular steel "cell" matrix up to 80 feet tall, and an AI-driven operating system that plans routes, resolves conflicts and dynamically reconfigures the matrix to store and retrieve anything from cases to full 3,000 lb pallets. The company raised a $120M Series C led by Avenir Growth in January 2026 (roughly $200M total) and sells the system as installed industrial infrastructure to enterprise distribution and food-and-beverage operators. Mytra publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Nomagic
providers.description: Nomagic builds Physical AI for end-to-end warehouse automation, using AI-powered robotic arms and computer vision to automate picking, packing, sorting and other fulfillment tasks across e-commerce, fashion, pharmaceutical and third-party logistics warehouses. Nomagic exposes a standard Station API for systems integrators, WCS/WMS providers and customers to control its robots, and a Grip AI API that adds an intelligence layer to third-party robot hardware; all robot actions are recorded to the Nomagic Cloud to continually improve its models. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures. Public developer documentation for these APIs is not published; integration is arranged directly with Nomagic.

providers.name: Symbotic
providers.description: Symbotic is an AI-powered warehouse automation company that designs, manufactures, and operates end-to-end robotic distribution and micro-fulfillment systems for food and beverage, retail grocery, healthcare, apparel, retail general merchandise, and consumer packaged goods customers. Its portfolio includes the Symbotic distribution solution for case handling, SymMicro for less-than-case micro-fulfillment, autonomous SymBots mobile robots, warehouse AI software, and Warehouse-as-a-Service offerings. Symbotic operates as a hardware-and-services vendor and does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs.

providers.name: Thirdwave
providers.description: Thirdwave (Third Wave Automation) builds autonomous material-handling systems for warehouses and distribution centers, led by its shared-autonomy forklift platform where one human operator can supervise a fleet of self-driving forklifts that operate independently and hand control back to a person when needed. Its ArmadaFMS (Armada Fleet Management System) software coordinates the robotic fleet across facilities. The company is a venture-backed logistics-robotics provider (backed by Homebrew and Norwest Venture Partners). As of this enrichment pass Third Wave publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: WeRide
providers.description: WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD) is an autonomous driving technology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Guangzhou, China. It develops Level 4 self-driving technology across a portfolio of five core products — Robotaxi, Robobus, Robovan, Robosweeper (autonomous sanitation) and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) — and operates its fleets in more than 40 cities across 12 countries. WeRide does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web presence and domain-security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Wheelocity
providers.description: Wheelocity (Wheelocity Fresh Private Limited) is a Bangalore, India based logistics and supply-chain company building daily fresh-produce and grocery delivery networks for underserved rural markets across India, which it frames as "the access rails for Bharat commerce." Its phygital (online plus offline) model combines location intelligence, IoT hardware, cold-chain and predictive demand forecasting with an electric-vehicle first-mile and last-mile fleet and a consumer app branded WoW. The company reports serving more than one million households, running over 100,000 km of EV movement daily and avoiding tens of thousands of kilograms of produce waste each day. Wheelocity is a venture-backed operating company (Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio) and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Relay Payments
providers.description: Relay Payments operates a secure digital payment network purpose-built for the freight and trucking industry. Its mobile app and platform let carriers, owner-operators, brokers, and merchants transact contactlessly for diesel fuel, lumper (dock unloading) fees, scales, parking, truck repairs, and freight payments between brokers and carriers, replacing cash, fleet checks, and legacy fuel cards while reducing fraud and streamlining back-office reconciliation. Relay is backed by Ribbit Capital. Partner/system integration is offered under a Relay System Integration Agreement, with developer documentation gated behind partner authentication at docs.relaypayments.com; no public API specification is currently published.

providers.name: Zauber
providers.description: Zauber is an AI agent platform purpose-built for sea and air freight forwarding operations. Freight forwarders describe their processes in plain language and Zauber's AI agents execute them consistently across global operations, automating rate and booking workflows with exception handling, deploying global workflows with local execution, and giving operators real-time operational visibility into conversion rates, response times, and exception patterns. The platform integrates with existing systems including Office 365, CargoWise One, carrier portals, and proprietary tooling. Zauber is a portfolio company of Point Nine. No public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's identity and security posture.

providers.name: Cyngn
providers.description: Cyngn (NASDAQ: CYN) is a Mountain View, California autonomous vehicle technology company that develops and deploys industrial autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for material handling. Its flagship DriveMod stack is a vehicle-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy system that retrofits onto standard industrial vehicles such as tuggers and forklifts, paired with the Cyngn Insight fleet-management, teleoperation, and analytics platform and the Cyngn Evolve data toolkit — together marketed as the Enterprise Autonomy Suite. Cyngn targets warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics operators facing labor shortages and safety challenges, and integrates with major warehouse management systems (Manhattan, Blue Yonder, SAP EWM). The company traces its corporate lineage to Cyanogen Inc. (the CyanogenMod company), whose dormant GitHub organization still links to cyngn.com.

providers.name: Lizee
providers.description: Lizee is a Paris-based Retail-as-a-Service platform that helps brands and retailers launch and operate circular commerce programs — rental, resale, and second-hand — end to end. Its stack pairs a rental platform, a resale/e-commerce platform, and a logistics platform (returns, refurbishment, reverse logistics) behind an operations API so a brand can offer rent or buy-back experiences on top of its existing catalog. Lizee runs a production API (api.lizee.io) and publishes a public Atlassian Statuspage, though it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs — the API surface is partner and integration facing. Lizee was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Speedinvest.

providers.name: Pickle Robot
providers.description: Pickle Robot builds Physical AI systems for supply chain automation, best known for autonomous truck- and container-unloading robots that handle non-palletized, floor-loaded freight. Its Dill Autonomy Engine (DAE) pairs classical optimal control with generative AI and foundation models, driving an industrial arm with vision, LiDAR, and an air-suction gripper to unload 400-1,500 cases per hour. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in the Boston, Massachusetts area, the company deploys into existing warehouses in days with no WMS integration and counts UPS among its customers. Pickle Robot exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sereact
providers.description: Sereact GmbH is a Stuttgart, Germany based physical-AI company building intelligent robotic systems for warehouse and fulfillment automation. Its "Cortex" platform pairs a Vision Language Action Model (VLAM) with robot control so robots can pick, place, sort, induct, and inspect diverse items in production without task-specific retraining, running across 50+ deployments in Europe and the US. Products include Pick-and-Place, Putwall, Induction, Bin Handling, Returns Handling, and the Lens perception system. Backed by Creandum and Point Nine; announced a $110M Series B. Sereact does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — an internal api.sereact.ai host exists but is a placeholder. This profile captures the company identity and public web/GitHub surface.

providers.name: Covariant
providers.description: Covariant is an Emeryville, California warehouse-robotics AI company founded in 2017 (originally as Embodied Intelligence) by UC Berkeley professor Pieter Abbeel and his former students Peter Chen, Rocky Duan, and Tianhao Zhang. The company builds the Covariant Brain, a universal AI platform that enables industrial picking robots to handle virtually any SKU regardless of shape, size, or packaging, and in March 2024 it introduced RFM-1 (Robotics Foundation Model 1), an 8-billion-parameter multimodal transformer trained on text, images, video, robot actions, and numerical sensor readings to give robots human-like reasoning over the physical world. Covariant ships AI-powered solutions for order picking, sortation, item induction, kitting, depalletization, and goods-to-person workflows, delivered through long-running integration partnerships with KNAPP (Pick-it-Easy Robot, since 2020) and ABB (warehouse robotics, since 2020), as well as deployments with retailers and logistics providers worldwide. In August 2024, Amazon announced a non-exclusive license to Covariant's robotic foundation models and hired its three co-founders along with roughly a quarter of its workforce in a reverse-acquihire arrangement; Covariant continues to operate independently under COO-turned-CEO Ted Stinson and co-founder Tianhao Zhang. The Covariant Brain and RFM-1 are proprietary, deployed on-premise on partner robotics hardware, and the company has no public developer API, SDK, open-source release, or third-party developer program.

providers.name: Terawatt Infrastructure
providers.description: Terawatt Infrastructure is a US infrastructure company that acquires, develops, owns, and operates purpose-built electric-vehicle charging centers for commercial fleets — medium- and heavy-duty trucking, drayage, autonomous vehicle and rideshare operators. The company sells charging-as-a-service rather than software: it holds real estate and grid interconnection, builds high-power charging sites (including the I-10 electrified corridor and sites near the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach), and runs them with its own proprietary Charge Management Software, operations and maintenance program, and a customer reservations portal. Terawatt states publicly that it has implemented the Open Charge Point Interface (OCPI) with custom extensions so fleet customers get visibility into its charging facilities, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract for that surface.

providers.name: Woowa Brothers
providers.description: Woowa Brothers is the Seoul-based technology company behind Baedal Minjok (Baemin), South Korea's leading food delivery platform, alongside B-Mart quick commerce, Baemin Connect rider services, and robotics initiatives for serving and delivery robots. A subsidiary of Delivery Hero since 2021, the company runs a strong engineering culture through its Woowahan tech blog and first-party open-source libraries on GitHub (NestJS libraries, WoowahanJS, Redis tooling), but it does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Grubmarket
providers.description: GrubMarket is a food technology company founded in 2014 that digitally transforms the American food supply chain across the U.S. and Canada. It operates a B2B wholesale eCommerce marketplace connecting buyers to thousands of food products, an AI-powered ERP and warehouse-management software suite (WholesaleWare) for food distributors and growers, and a direct-to-consumer farm-fresh food delivery service. Backed by Battery Ventures, GGV Capital, and Y Combinator, GrubMarket was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass GrubMarket publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: AI Fleet
providers.description: Aifleet (aifleet.com) is a technology-driven, full-stack trucking carrier founded in 2020 and headquartered in Austin, Texas. The company describes itself as the first full-stack, AI-driven carrier, pairing company drivers with proprietary AI algorithms and its own Transportation Management System (TMS) to optimize truck utilization, routing, load matching, fuel usage, and scheduling across the roughly $400B U.S. freight sector. Aifleet emphasizes a driver-centric model — better pay, predictable schedules, and reduced wait times — alongside shipper-facing services with proactive tracking updates and predictive ETAs. It has raised roughly $50M since founding (Series A 2021, venture round 2023, Series B 2024) from investors including Obvious Ventures, Ibex Investors, Volvo Group Venture Capital, Compound, and Heron Rock. Aifleet is a logistics service provider rather than a developer-facing API platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: DEFCON AI
providers.description: DEFCON AI is a modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A) company based in McLean, Virginia, building AI-driven optimization for contested logistics and mobility across defense and commercial operations. Founded in 2022, it develops mission-tailored optimization and intelligent-agent simulation products - including ARTIV (delivered to U.S. Air Force Air Mobility Command) and R-ALIGN for resilient multimodal logistics - that let planners rapidly generate and evaluate mission scenarios in dynamic, disrupted environments. The company was awarded a five-year, $115M prototype agreement supporting U.S. Marine Corps logistics modernization. DEFCON AI publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Fernride
providers.description: FERNRIDE (FERNRIDE GmbH) is a Munich, Germany based ground-autonomy company delivering human-assisted autonomous driving for logistics. Its platform automates electric and diesel trucks and terminal tractors across container terminals, yard operations, manufacturing supply, defence logistics, and open-road trucking, pairing on-vehicle autonomy with remote human oversight (teleoperation) for reliability at scale. A centralized Management Suite lets fleet managers monitor and control the autonomous fleet and integrates with existing terminal operating systems (TOS) and yard management systems (YMS). Customers and partners have included DB Schenker, Volkswagen, HHLA, and NVIDIA. FERNRIDE was acquired by Quantum Systems in December 2025. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest; the company exposes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Lydia AI
providers.description: Lydia AI is an enterprise AI company whose flagship platform, ORCA, reasons through complex operational problems and delivers structured work product rather than chat replies. ORCA spans three domains: Content & Commerce (generating product content, campaign assets, and structured search data), Evidence & Analysis (analyzing large document sets for legal discovery), and Operations & Logistics (optimizing routing, dispatch, and disruption response). The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Lydia AI exposes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface; engagement is via a book-a-demo/contact sales motion.

providers.name: Wise Systems
providers.description: Wise Systems provides autonomous routing and last-mile delivery optimization software powered by machine learning. Its platform helps fleet operators plan strategy, optimize and dynamically re-route deliveries, dispatch in real time, track driver performance, and improve last-mile efficiency across industries including auto parts, beverage, building materials, container management, field service, food service, healthcare, linen services, parcel/courier, and retail. Wise Systems exposes an internal "Engine API" during customer implementations to connect data inputs and outputs, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs. Backed by Techstars and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

providers.name: Gatik
providers.description: Gatik is an autonomous trucking company founded in 2017 by Gautam Narang, Arjun Narang and Apeksha Kumavat, headquartered in Silicon Valley, California. Gatik builds and operates the Gatik Driver, an SAE Level 4 autonomy system purpose-built for the middle mile: short-haul, repeatable freight routes between distribution centers, dark stores and retail endpoints. Gatik runs driverless medium-duty box trucks in commercial service for Fortune 50 retailers and grocers including Walmart, Loblaw, Kroger, Tyson Foods, Pitney Bowes and PepsiCo, across Texas, Arkansas, Arizona, Ontario and other North American markets. The company partners with Isuzu, Ryder, Goodyear and NVIDIA, runs the Gatik Arena simulation platform, and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK or developer portal — its surface is a corporate marketing site plus a legacy archive site carrying about, safety, news, careers and legal pages.

providers.name: Flycrates
providers.description: Flycrates is an international shipping service, founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, that lets shoppers outside the United States buy US Amazon.com Prime items and have them delivered worldwide. Instead of filling an Amazon cart, customers fill a fixed-size crate (small, medium, or large); Flycrates then purchases the items, consolidates them, clears customs, and pays import duty and tax on the buyer's behalf before shipping via DHL, FedEx, or UPS to more than 117 countries. It also offers a Chrome browser extension that adds "Add to Flycrates" buttons directly onto Amazon product pages. Flycrates raised a seed round led by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a consumer web application only and exposes no public API, developer portal, or partner integration program.

providers.name: Konga
providers.description: Konga is a Lagos, Nigeria-based e-commerce company founded in July 2012 and now operating as Nigeria's leading online shopping marketplace, combining a first-party retail business with a third-party seller marketplace across consumer electronics, mobile phones, home appliances, fashion, groceries, beauty, and lifestyle categories. Konga runs a vertically integrated stack alongside its storefront: KongaPay, a Central Bank of Nigeria-licensed and NDIC-insured payments platform offering checkout, transfers, virtual accounts, multi-currency wallets, POS, bill payments, savings, and merchant payouts; Konga Travel & Tours, an IATA-certified travel agency providing flight bookings, hotels, and vacation packages; Konga Health (Medical Direct); Konga Foods/Groceries; KongaNow same-day delivery; and KXpress Logistics for nationwide fulfillment. Konga's revenue model spans marketplace commissions, first-party retail margin, KongaPay transaction fees, logistics fees, travel agency commissions, and seller advertising. Konga does not operate a unified public developer program: the marketplace exposes no documented public REST API for orders, products, or sellers; KongaPay published Android, iOS, and WooCommerce SDKs and SDK docs at kongapay.github.io, but that GitHub organization was archived on July 1, 2023, and the current KPay aggregator API documentation lives at kpayment-org.gitbook.io with limited public surface area focused on POS, Web Payment Gateway, Virtual Account, and Payment Link integrations for approved merchants. As a result, Konga is profiled here as a provider index rather than as an actively documented public-API company.

providers.name: Savi Technology
providers.description: Savi Technology provides Internet of Things (IoT) and active RFID (aRFID) solutions for real-time supply chain visibility, asset tracking, and cargo security.
