Combining active RFID tags, environmental condition sensors, and machine intelligence, Savi delivers location, condition, and estimated-time- of-arrival data for cargo and high-value assets across government, military (including U.S. Department of Defense in-transit visibility), and commercial supply chains. The company is headquartered in Wilmington, North Carolina. As of this enrichment pass, Savi Technology exposes no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDKs, or documented web API; its only authenticated surface is the aRFID-VI customer catalog (savirfidcatalog.net).

providers.name: Shippio
providers.description: Shippio is a Japanese logistics-technology company positioning itself as "Japan's first digital forwarder." It provides cloud-based SaaS for visualizing and streamlining international trade and freight-forwarding operations, combining domain expertise with AI-era digital technology. Its product line includes Shippio Forwarding (a digital forwarding service), Shippio Cargo (trade-management SaaS for shippers/importers-exporters), and Shippio Works (trade-management SaaS for logistics operators), delivered through a multi-sided platform that connects shippers and operators. The company is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Shippio publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or pricing; its APIs are internal platform APIs referenced only in engineering job postings, so this profile is identity-only with no public API surface.

providers.name: Apptronik
providers.description: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas-based humanoid robotics company founded in 2016 as a spinout from the Human Centered Robotics Lab at the University of Texas at Austin. Co-founded by Jeff Cardenas (CEO), Dr. Nick Paine (CTO), and Dr. Luis Sentis (scientific advisor), the company designs and manufactures Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot standing 5'8", weighing 160 lbs, capable of lifting 55 lbs, and running for roughly 4 hours on a swappable battery. Apollo targets warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics applications including trailer unloading, case picking, palletization, machine tending, and workcell delivery. Apptronik has commercial pilot programs and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz (automotive manufacturing logistics), GXO Logistics (multi-phase R&D in U.S. distribution centers), Jabil (supply-chain partner helping scale production and an internal Apollo deployment), and Google DeepMind (Apollo integrates Gemini Robotics vision-language-action models). The company previously built NASA's Valkyrie humanoid and ten-plus other research robots. As of February 2026 Apptronik had raised more than $935M (including a $520M Series A-X extension) at a reported $5B valuation, with investors including B Capital, Google, and Mercedes-Benz. The company sells/leases Apollo to enterprise customers via a direct contact-sales motion and ships a proprietary "point-and-click" control suite for deploying solutions; there is no public developer portal, no published REST/AsyncAPI/gRPC API, no public SDK, no open-source release, and no public GitHub repositories under the `apptronik` org.

providers.name: XPO
providers.description: XPO, Inc. (NYSE: XPO) is a Fortune 500 transportation company and one of the largest providers of less-than-truckload (LTL) freight transportation in North America. Following the spin-offs of GXO Logistics (contract logistics, 2021) and RXO (brokerage, 2022), XPO is now a pure-play LTL trucking company operating a network of service centers across the United States and Mexico. XPO does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; customer integrations (rate quotes, shipment tracking, EDI) are arranged through enterprise account managers and standard EDI exchanges.

providers.name: XPO Logistics
providers.description: XPO Logistics, Inc. is a leading provider of less-than-truckload (LTL) transportation in North America. The company offers freight transportation through a proprietary network of service centers and uses technology to drive efficiency for more than 50,000 customers. XPO Logistics historically operated as part of XPO, Inc. (NYSE: XPO), the publicly traded company that spun off GXO Logistics (contract logistics) in 2021 and RXO (brokerage) in 2022, leaving XPO focused on LTL trucking. XPO Logistics does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integrations are arranged through enterprise account managers.

providers.name: Haladir
providers.description: Haladir is a Y Combinator-backed startup building a decisional AI platform for logistics operations. Describing itself as "the decisional AI layer for logistics," Haladir unifies fragmented operational data from existing warehouse management (WMS), transportation management (TMS), and order management (OMS) systems into a single operational graph, then applies constraint-optimization solvers and machine-learning models to automate supply chain decisions across routing, picking, labor allocation, and inventory. Its approach treats large language models as formalization tools that translate messy operational rules into precise constraints for traditional solvers, rather than as decision-makers. Target customers include third-party logistics providers (3PLs), contract logistics providers, distributors, and shippers managing global supply chains. The company has raised $4.3M in seed funding led by BoxGroup and Susa Ventures. This profile currently exposes no public API or developer documentation; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: APX
providers.description: APX (APX Logistics Solutions) is a Southeast Asian less-than-truckload (LTL) digital logistics platform headquartered in Bangkok, with operations in Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore. It positions itself as the region's first LTL digital logistics provider, offering domestic and cross-border shipping, international sea and air freight, customs brokerage, warehousing and distribution, project logistics, and heavy-lift/breakbulk services. Its proprietary technology platform provides online shipment booking, real-time tracking with ETA notifications, digital proof-of-delivery, AI-assisted route optimization, a driver app, and analytics dashboards including CO2/ESG reporting. APX is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass APX publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; shipment tracking is currently integrable only via third-party aggregators.

providers.name: Inventa
providers.description: Inventa is a Brazilian B2B commerce platform — a "B2B commerce cloud" — that integrates technology, credit, and logistics on a single platform so brands and distributors can scale wholesale sales in Brazil. Its products include a sales platform that syncs catalogs, orders, inventory, and prices across B2B e-commerce sites and marketplaces via ERP integrations; a field-sales mobile app for sellers; automated credit analysis and approval; shared distribution-center logistics (OMS/WMS/TMS) with fulfillment and 72-hour delivery in the São Paulo region; multichannel customer support; and business-intelligence dashboards. Solution packages span Fulfillment, Response, FullService, and a pay-per-use OnDemand model. The company is headquartered in São Paulo. Inventa configures the API and connector integrations for its customers rather than publishing a public developer portal, so it has no public API artifacts as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Kiva Systems (Amazon Robotics since 2012)
providers.description: Kiva Systems was a warehouse robotics company founded in 2003 that pioneered the goods-to-person mobile fulfillment model, in which fleets of low-profile drive units lift and carry mobile storage pods to human pick stations instead of moving workers to static shelving. Amazon acquired Kiva Systems in March 2012 for approximately US$775 million and renamed it Amazon Robotics in 2015. Since the acquisition the technology has been developed exclusively for Amazon's own fulfillment and sortation network and is no longer sold to third parties. Amazon Robotics publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; amazonrobotics.com now redirects to Amazon's internal identity provider and kivasystems.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical and acquisition record in the physical-AI and warehouse-robotics space rather than as an integratable API provider. Not to be confused with AWS RoboMaker or AWS IoT RoboRunner, which are AWS product APIs.

providers.name: Meituan
providers.description: Meituan (美团) is a Chinese technology-retail company operating one of the world's largest on-demand local-services and food-delivery super-apps. Its platform spans restaurant food delivery, in-store dining and group buying (Dianping), grocery and instant retail, hotel and travel booking, bike and moped sharing, and payments. Meituan runs a partner/developer cooperation center exposing merchant, delivery/logistics, and local-services integration APIs to business partners; these are partner-gated and documented in Chinese, with no public OpenAPI specification, SDK registry, or self-serve developer signup surfaced at this time.

providers.name: Nimble Robotics
providers.description: Nimble Robotics (Nimble) is an autonomous robotic third-party logistics (3PL) company building AI-powered robots that pick, pack, and fulfill ecommerce orders with minimal human intervention. Founded by Simon Kalouche, the company operates fully autonomous robotic fulfillment centers and is training general-purpose robot AI to power fast, economical commerce. Backed by Accel and partnered with FedEx, Nimble raised a $106M Series C at a $1B valuation, with board member Marc Raibert (Boston Dynamics founder). Nimble is a physical robotics and logistics operator and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Retailo
providers.description: Retailo (Retailo Technologies) operates a B2B marketplace that helps independent retailers across the MENAP region (Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan) restock their shops, offering thousands of products, instant price comparisons and next-day delivery through the Retailo App. Its ecosystem also includes the Hisaab App, a fintech and bookkeeping product for merchants, and HORECA supply services for the hospitality trade. Founded by Talha Ansari, Muhammad Nowkhaiz and Wahaj Ahmed and backed by 500 Global, the company is operational in markets including the UAE and Pakistan. Retailo distributes its products as native iOS and Android mobile applications and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: RIVR
providers.description: RIVR (RIVR Technologies AG, formerly Swiss-Mile) is a Swiss robotics and AI company spun out of ETH Zurich that develops autonomous legged-wheeled robots for doorstep delivery across parcel, grocery, and instant food/convenience segments. RIVR pursues "General Physical AI" by combining large-scale reinforcement learning in simulation with real-world self-supervised learning from live delivery operations, owning the full stack from software to hardware for reliability, safety, and cost efficiency. The company operates commercial deployments with partners including Just Eat Takeaway.com, Swiss Post, Migros Online, Evri, and Veho, and is backed by investors including Hongshan and Bezos Expeditions. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record; RIVR publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Donkey
providers.description: Donkey is an AI-native trading company (Y Combinator, Summer 2026) that buys directly from Chinese factories and sells delivered duty-paid to US importers. Donkey mines public US customs records to identify the factory that actually makes a product, returns a landed DDP quote within 72 hours, runs its own on-the-floor quality inspections before the factory is paid, clears customs, moves the money, and offers credit-insured net-45 terms to qualified buyers. Founded by Benjamin Martindale (CEO) and Minghao Tan (CTO), the company runs small teams in San Francisco and China. Donkey publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform today; this profile tracks its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Flytrex
providers.description: Flytrex is an autonomous drone delivery operator headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, with US operations centered on the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and North Carolina. The company runs an end-to-end backyard delivery service that flies food and small goods from partner restaurants and retailers to consumer homes in roughly five minutes, operating its own Sky-series multirotor aircraft, ground docks, and a remote-operations control center. Flytrex sells to consumers through its own iOS and Android ordering apps and to merchants through a partner portal, and routes demand from third-party marketplaces including DoorDash and Uber Eats. It does not currently publish a public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Beeline Bikes
providers.description: Beeline Bikes (now operating as Beeline Connect) is a B2B software platform for the bicycle industry that links riders, retailers, and brands across North America, with roughly 3,300 participating retailers. The platform provides real-time service scheduling and 24/7 appointment booking, live market inventory management, test-ride booking, local bicycle assembly coordination, warranty submission and reimbursement tracking, an affiliate e-commerce sales channel with revenue sharing to local dealers, and a dynamic dealer locator. It supports both mobile and in-shop retail operations and serves established brands such as Aventon, Priority, Lectric, and Pedego. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or integration surface has been found at this time.

providers.name: NEO TECH MOBILITY HOLDINGS LIMITED
providers.description: NEO TECH MOBILITY HOLDINGS LIMITED (Neo Mobility) is a UAE-based B2B electric-mobility startup driving sustainable transportation across the MENA region. Neo bundles electric-vehicle fleets, charging infrastructure, an integrated fleet/driver/operations/energy management platform, driver-safety programs, and human-capital support into a single subscription-based ecosystem — delivering EV Delivery-as-a-Service for e-commerce, food delivery, and last-mile logistics, alongside e-taxi mobility. The company publishes no public developer or API program; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network discovery.

providers.name: Vendease
providers.description: Vendease is a Nigerian B2B food procurement platform (founded 2020, Y Combinator W21, backed by Partech Africa and TLcom) that helps restaurants, hotels, and other food businesses buy fresh and processed food supplies, offering Buy Now, Pay Later financing, supplier consolidation, cold-chain logistics, and 24-hour delivery in Lagos. Vendease publishes no public developer API or SDKs; its procurement, payments, inventory, and tenant management service APIs are internal-only, though its engineering handover documentation is publicly available on GitHub.

1919 (壹玖壹玖 / 1919酒类直供) is a Chengdu-based Chinese alcoholic-beverage retail and supply-chain platform operated by Sichuan 1919 Wines & Spirits SCM Co., Ltd. Founded in 2006, it runs an omnichannel online-to-offline model: the 1919吃喝 consumer app and a third-party e-commerce matrix layered on more than 3,000 franchised stores across 1,000+ Chinese cities, marketed on a 19-minute rapid-delivery promise, alongside a B2B liquor supply-chain business selling order management, logistics and data-marketing services to distributors. The company listed on China's NEEQ board in 2014 (830993), took a RMB 2 billion strategic investment from Alibaba in 2018, and delisted from NEEQ in 2023; its shares now change hands on private secondary marketplaces.

providers.name: cargo.one
providers.description: cargo.one is a Berlin-headquartered digital freight platform that operates as an AI-native operating system for air and ocean freight logistics. The platform unifies freight forwarder operations by centralizing rates, partners, and systems on a single end-to-end surface shared between human teams and AI agents. For freight forwarders, cargo.one provides air e-booking with 76+ integrated airlines (300+ total network), ocean freight rate management with 10+ liner integrations, multimodal quoting across air, ocean, road, and local charges, a Rate Management System for buy/sell/internal rates, a branded 24/7 self-service Customer Portal, analytics dashboards, a 24/7 Global Network for cross-timezone quoting, and an API Suite with native TMS integrations for CargoWise, Cargospot, and Descartes. For carriers, cargo.one delivers a market-intelligence and customer-access platform spanning the end-to-end commercial cycle. AI workflows are offered in three deployment modes — Co-pilot (approval-based), Supervised (autonomous with escalation), and Autonomous — covering rate management, rate procurement, quoting, booking, and customer support automation, backed by retrieval-augmented generation and a cargo.one MCP Server for custom solutions. Notable customers include Lufthansa Cargo, Kuehne+Nagel, DSV, Maersk, CMA CGM, Hellmann, and Rhenus Logistics. cargo.one's API and TMS integrations are partner / enterprise offerings — there is no public self-serve OpenAPI specification, developer sandbox, or open-source SDK published outside of customer onboarding.

providers.name: Dayjob
providers.description: Dayjob is an AI-powered scheduling agent built for waste management and skip hire fleets, operated by Gaea Technology Ltd and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026). Its autonomous agents analyze millions of potential route combinations to build optimized daily schedules that factor in travel times, skip sizes, driver availability and priority job assignments, then continuously re-optimize in real time as new jobs, driver changes and exceptions arrive. Dayjob integrates with existing ERP and telematics systems (Weighsoft, PurGo, Wastelogics, plus custom report setups) and claims customers see revenue and efficiency gains, tighter time-window hit rates and materially less planning admin. It is a vertical logistics application rather than an API platform - no public developer portal, API reference or SDKs are published at this time. This profile has been enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Pyka
providers.description: Pyka is an Alameda, California company that designs and manufactures large, dual-use heavy-lift autonomous electric aircraft for commercial and defense operations. Its flagship products are the Pelican 2 autonomous crop-protection aircraft for aerial application and the DropShip long-range heavy-lift cargo UAS. Pyka builds a fully integrated, vertically owned autonomy stack — an Autonomy Engine (real-time OS, sensor fusion, flight control, and path planning), a Mission Control operator suite (simulation, communications, and operator interface), and custom aerospace-grade hardware. The company is backed by DCVC and Obvious Ventures. Pyka does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint. Surfaced via VC portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: REEF
providers.description: REEF Technology operates a network of urban logistics and proximity real-estate locations, transforming underutilized spaces such as parking lots into multi-purpose neighborhood hubs for goods, services, and experiences. Through its "Power of Proximity" model and its Ulysses operator program, REEF connects brands, cloud/ghost kitchens, delivery, and mobility services to local consumers while helping property owners diversify revenue. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, REEF is a logistics and real-estate operator; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: MoveitPro
providers.description: MoveitPro (MoveitPro+) is web-based moving company management software built by professional movers, covering the full operation of a moving and storage company - CRM and lead capture, estimating and quoting, a smart dispatch board with drag-and-drop scheduling and crew assignment, fleet and maintenance management, digital bills of lading and e-signatures, itemized inventory, storage and warehouse tracking, invoicing and credit-card payments, commission tracking, and AI call transcription and QA. MoveitPro advertises "Open API & Custom Integrations" and ships native integrations (QuickBooks, Twilio, Mailchimp, Google Maps/Calendar), but does not publish a self-serve public developer API, reference documentation, or OpenAPI. Its only publicly documented programmatic surface is a Zapier integration exposing Clients, Leads, Jobs, and Estimates. The APIs listed below are logical resources modeled from that documented Zapier integration; MoveitPro does not publish HTTP endpoints, base URLs, or authentication details.

providers.name: Alchemize
providers.description: Alchemize is an AI-enabled customs brokerage that automates import compliance workflows for importers. The Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company pairs licensed customs expertise with artificial intelligence to answer regulatory and tariff questions in minutes rather than days, reduce manual data-entry errors before shipments reach the port, and give importers a single view of every shipment, status, and communication via API, EDI, or web portal. Founded by Robert Hou (previously Confido, YC) and Samuel Fu (previously Netflix), Alchemize targets inefficiency in the $30B+ customs brokerage industry with an AI-native compliance and trade-operations platform.

providers.name: CSX Corporation
providers.description: CSX Corporation is a Class I freight railroad operating one of the largest rail networks in the eastern United States, serving 23 states with roughly 20,000 route miles of track. CSX moves bulk commodities, intermodal shipments, and merchandise for industrial customers and operates the ShipCSX customer portal for shipment management, EDI integration, and freight tracking.

providers.name: Dada
providers.description: Dada Group (Dada Nexus, NASDAQ: DADA) is a leading Chinese instant retail and local on-demand delivery platform, headquartered in Shanghai and founded in 2014. It operates an open, crowdsourced delivery network of more than one million rider partners serving supermarkets, pharmacies, fresh-food and restaurant merchants across thousands of counties and cities, alongside merchant fulfillment products such as the Haibo in-store logistics system and the Dada Youjian picking service. Now integrated into the JD.com ecosystem, its core delivery brand was rebranded to JD Instant Delivery (京东秒送) in May 2024. Dada runs a merchant Open Platform (开放平台) for order, delivery-tracking and fulfillment integrations. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company
providers.description: MSC (Mediterranean Shipping Company) is a privately-held, family-owned global container shipping and logistics group headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, founded in 1970 by Gianluigi Aponte and now led by CEO Soren Toft under the Aponte-Diamant family. MSC is the world's largest container shipping line by fleet size and capacity, operating roughly 900 cargo vessels with a combined intake of about 7 million TEU and controlling more than a fifth of global container capacity as of late 2025. The carrier offers a portfolio of digital shipment-management products through its myMSC e-business platform — including Instant Quote for online rate generation, online booking, electronic Bill of Lading and Sea Waybill issuance via eDocs, container Track & Trace, and the myMSC mobile app — and exposes a Direct Integrations program for shippers, freight forwarders, and NVOCCs that combines REST APIs and EDI message exchange. The MSC Developer Portal (developerportal.msc.com), hosted on Microsoft Azure API Management, publishes documentation and EDI message implementation guides for products such as the DCSA-aligned Track & Trace API (v1.2 and v2.2), Booking, Booking Confirmation (X12 301 / EDIFACT IFTMIN), and Shipping Instructions, alongside ANSI X12 and EDIFACT IFTMIN / IFTMBC / COPRAR reference documents. MSC also runs direct-integration partnerships with INTTRA, Infor Nexus, and CargoSmart. API and EDI access is not self-service: prospective integrators must submit a Direct Integration request, and fees may apply.

providers.name: Tezbor, Inc.
providers.description: Tezbor is a Tashkent, Uzbekistan based courier and last-mile logistics company that automates the delivery of documents, parcels, and cargo across Uzbekistan. Beyond its consumer and business courier service, Tezbor operates a technology platform that exposes delivery ordering and tracking through an integration API, ready-made e-commerce plugins (WooCommerce, OpenCart, Magento), mobile apps, dashboards, and Telegram bots, so that any online store can automatically generate a Tezbor delivery order from each purchase. The company is backed by 500 Global, Activat, and StartupBase, and counts brands such as Beeline, Ozon, and OQ among its delivery clients.

providers.name: Xiaopangxiong
providers.description: Xiaopangxiong (小胖熊, "small fat bear") is a Chinese B2B e-commerce platform for home and office renovation materials, operated by Shanghai Miju Network Technology Co., Ltd. (上海米居网络科技有限公司). The platform connects building-material suppliers with renovation contractors, crew foremen, and decoration companies, selling the full range of auxiliary materials (辅材) — sand, cement, paint and coatings, electrical wiring, pipes, tiles, and leveling supplies — through a self-operated model that spans factory-direct procurement, warehousing, logistics, delivery, installation, and after-sales service. Headquartered in Shanghai with service stations and warehouses in Suzhou, Hangzhou, Hefei, Ningbo, Wuxi, and Jiaxing, Xiaopangxiong is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and distributes primarily through its 小胖熊 mobile app; the company publishes no public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services
providers.description: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd. (NYSE: ZIM) is a global container liner shipping company founded in 1945 and headquartered in Haifa, Israel. ZIM operates in more than 90 countries, serving over 30,000 customers across more than 300 ports worldwide with a differentiated global-niche strategy focused on agile fleet management and select trade lanes. The company is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange and, as of 2026, is the subject of a pending acquisition by Hapag-Lloyd at approximately $35.00 per share. ZIM's digital surface includes the myZIM customer area, ZIMonitor cargo visibility, an electronic Bill of Lading (eB/L) service, a Draft B/L tool, EDI integrations for booking and shipping instructions, a mobile application, and a developer API portal at api.zim.com hosted on Microsoft Azure API Management. Access to the ZIM API requires registering through ZIM API Support and obtaining a security token; rate limits are set per organization at registration. No public OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or GitHub organization are published, so ZIM is profiled here as a Tier-3 catalog entry pending spec disclosure or partner access.

providers.name: Aerialoop
providers.description: Aerialoop is a drone technology and urban logistics company that designs, builds, and operates intelligent aerial networks for cargo delivery, surveillance, and infrastructure inspection. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Miami with operations rooted in Quito, Ecuador, it is one of the fastest-growing drone delivery operations in Latin America. Its ALT 6-8 delivery drone carries a 5kg payload for urban logistics, while the ALT 6-ISR line adds HD, infrared, and night-vision cameras with AI-powered intrusion detection; extended-range variants operate up to 120km using LEO satellite connectivity for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights. The company has completed over 50,000 flights across six countries. Aerialoop is a Techstars Miami (powered by J.P. Morgan) portfolio company. It currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD
providers.description: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD operates Moedatech (معداتك), Saudi Arabia's first digital procurement and rental marketplace for heavy construction equipment, connecting contractors with verified suppliers of excavators, cranes, and trucks through RFQs, real-time bidding, and audit-ready digital contracts. Founded in Riyadh in 2020 by Ali Merie and Mansour Hmaid, the company pairs the marketplace with a telematics/fleet layer (built on Traccar GPS tracking) so equipment owners can monitor real-time asset performance. The product ships as iOS and Android apps plus a web app; there is no publicly documented developer API at this time. The company is backed by 500 Global and Plug and Play Middle East. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from the company's public web, brand (moedatech.net), and GitHub presence.

providers.name: Logixboard
providers.description: Logixboard provides a unified, white-labeled customer experience platform for freight forwarders and logistics service providers, letting their customers book, track, quote, and manage shipments across ocean, air, FTL/LTL, customs, and warehousing from a single branded portal. It ingests and normalizes shipment data from TMS and WMS systems (CargoWise, Descartes, homegrown systems) via private API, file drop (FTP/SFTP), and database sync, so providers can differentiate on digital visibility. Logixboard exposes no public developer API; integrations are delivered as bespoke, provider-scoped data connections. Added to the API Evangelist network from the venture portfolios of Insight Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and Techstars.

providers.name: Warehousing1
providers.description: Warehousing1 is a Berlin-based LogTech company, founded in 2018 by Nico Szeli, Nils Aschmann and Fabian Sedlmayr, that operates a digital fulfillment and warehousing marketplace connecting brands and e-commerce merchants to an independent network of more than 1,000 logistics locations across Germany, Europe and the US. Its cloud platform and customer portal centralize warehousing, order picking, packing and shipping, and integrate with common ERP systems, online shops and marketplaces so companies can scale contract logistics, distribution and e-commerce fulfillment. The company has served 500+ customers and is backed by HV Capital, Schenker Ventures, Aster Capital and Wille Finance. Warehousing1 does not publish a public developer API; integration is delivered through managed ERP/shop connectors and its customer portal.

providers.name: Boxbot
providers.description: Boxbot builds next-generation supply chain automation, making logistics operations more productive, intelligent, and resilient through automated, high-density dynamic storage that unlocks new AI-driven capabilities. Its platform is designed for mission-control fulfillment facilities: real-time space allocation packs variable-sized items densely, hands-free load/unload moves items onto and off proprietary storage trays linked to standard conveyors with no pick or load stations, and a modular, gantry-based architecture delivers a robust, fault-tolerant design with no single point of failure. Boxbot is a hardware/robotics company backed by Playground Global; it publishes a marketing presence but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Evri
providers.description: Evri is the United Kingdom's largest dedicated parcel delivery company, formerly Hermes UK, headquartered in Leeds and majority owned by Apollo-managed funds. Following the CMA-cleared 2025 merger with DHL eCommerce UK, the combined group delivers more than a billion parcels a year across a courier network of 30,000+ couriers and van drivers, thousands of ParcelShops and lockers, and domestic, returns and international services for retailers and marketplace sellers. Evri sits at the last-mile end of the supply chain — the carrier a shipper, retailer or e-commerce platform hands a parcel to for final delivery in the UK. Its API posture is customer-contract portal only: Evri publishes no developer portal, no public API reference and no machine-readable specification. The host api.evri.com resolves to a live Tyk API Gateway (5.13.0) whose only publicly reachable path is an unauthenticated health check; every other probed path returns 404 and no listen path is discoverable without credentials. Shipment, label, ParcelShop, Print in Store and tracking credentials are issued by an Evri account manager or sales representative to contracted Corporate or Business accounts, with sandbox and production credentials handed over by email. In practice most integrators reach Evri indirectly through shipping-API aggregators such as EasyPost, ShipEngine / ShipStation, Sendcloud, AfterShip and Intersoft Sapient rather than directly.

providers.name: AutoStore
providers.description: AutoStore is a global warehouse robotics and technology company headquartered in Nedre Vats, Norway, that pioneered the cube storage automated storage and retrieval system (AS/RS). Its goods-to-person solution combines autonomous robots, an aluminum storage grid of stacked bins, workstation ports, and controlling software (marketed as CubeVerse, spanning design, simulation, operations, and predictive diagnostics) to fulfill orders in a fraction of the floor space of conventional warehouses. With more than 1,950 systems deployed across nearly 65 countries, AutoStore serves retail, grocery, 3PL, healthcare, and industrial customers. Systems are distributed, designed, installed, and serviced through a global network of qualified system integrators rather than a public developer/API program. AutoStore was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: BlackBuck
providers.description: BlackBuck, operated by Zinka Logistics Solutions and incorporated in 2015, runs India's largest digital trucking platform, digitizing the truck-operator lifecycle for roughly a million truck operators (about 28% of India's truckers) across 100,000+ villages. Its super-app spans a loads marketplace, FASTag toll payments, fuel, GPS/telematics, vehicle and working-capital financing, and a used-trucks marketplace. Listed on the NSE as BLACKBUCK since November 2024, the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer program, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment; this profile carries the company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Dimension
providers.description: Dimension is a nationwide, on-demand waste management and junk removal platform (formerly Trash Warrior) backed by 500 Global. It offers digital booking with instant AI-generated pricing (their "Mirror Mirror AI" quoter), same-day and next-day pickup for cardboard, appliances, mattresses, hazardous and medical waste, plus dumpster rentals, for both businesses and individuals. Every job includes tracking with detailed diversion data, receipts, and photos, and can be booked as a one-off or recurring service. Dimension has been awarded a State of California RFP contract for PPE waste removal. The company operates a customer-facing booking application and help center but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Movopack
providers.description: Movopack is a Milan-based sustainability startup, founded in 2021 and backed by Techstars, 360 Capital, and Greiner Innoventures, that provides reusable, customizable packaging for e-commerce, retail, and B2B logistics. Its circular system pairs branded reusable mailers with pre-paid return labels and QR-code drop-off points, then handles quality checks, cleaning, and redistribution — cutting packaging waste by up to 98% and CO2 emissions by 84% after repeated reuse cycles. Movopack is a physical-product and reverse-logistics company and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Slip Robotics
providers.description: Slip Robotics is an Atlanta, Georgia-based robotics company that builds SlipBots, autonomous omnidirectional Automated Loading Robots (ALRs) that load and unload any truck trailer in about five minutes without a forklift ever entering the trailer. Each SlipBot carries up to eight pallets and roughly six tons, cutting driver dwell time from around ninety minutes to five while reducing material-handling damage and loading-dock accidents. The company also offers SlipLift, a platform that extends autonomous trailer loading and unloading to heavier freight and regional and last-mile routes. Slip Robotics markets its robots-as-a-service offering as requiring no IT integration, is backed by DCVC, and won Best New Innovation in supply chain technology at MODEX 2024. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: TruKKer
providers.description: TruKKer is a tech-enabled logistics and transportation company serving businesses across the EMEA region. Its platform uses AI-driven freight matching and smart route visibility to connect shippers with carriers for land freight, cross-border transport, rent-by-trip, and home and office moving, alongside services such as ProcureCo and TruKKer Safe. TruKKer was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. During enrichment no public developer API, API documentation, SDK, CLI, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface was found on trukker.com; this profile captures the company's public web identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Buildcon
providers.description: Buildcon is a Belgrade-based construction and logistics digitalisation company that builds Buildx, a proprietary construction project management platform covering project scheduling, cost tracking, daily logs, installed-quantities tracking, and reporting, alongside Buildx Warehouse for warehouse management and Buildx Tracking for real-time asset tracking. The team pairs deep construction and logistics domain knowledge with a modern web stack (React, Angular, Node.js, PostgreSQL on AWS/DigitalOcean) to help builders and logistics operators move off spreadsheets and onto connected operational software. Buildcon is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: NGL Energy Partners
providers.description: NGL Energy Partners LP is a diversified midstream master limited partnership providing transportation, storage, blending, and marketing services for crude oil, natural gas liquids, refined products, and water solutions to producers and end-users across the energy industry. The company is publicly traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol NGL and operates three primary business units: Crude Oil Logistics, Water Solutions, and NGL Liquids.

providers.name: AptDeco
providers.description: AptDeco is a full-service online marketplace for buying and selling used, new, and vintage furniture. Founded in 2014 in New York City by Reham Fagiri and Kalam Dennis, the company handles the entire resale transaction end to end: pickup, disassembly and assembly, delivery, payment, scheduling, and logistics are all carried out by its own trained delivery teams. AptDeco serves the New York City metro, New Jersey, Connecticut, Philadelphia, Delaware, and the San Francisco Bay Area, and has expanded to additional US metros with national shipping. Backed by Y Combinator and Initialized Capital. AptDeco does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and developer surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TakeOff
providers.description: Takeoff Technologies, Inc. is an eGrocery micro-fulfillment company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. It paired KNAPP-built robotic storage-and-retrieval hardware with its own cloud software stack — order management, inventory, pick routing, labor management, and delivery orchestration — into micro-fulfillment centers (MFCs) installed inside or beside existing supermarkets, so grocers could assemble online orders in minutes instead of sending shoppers down the aisles. Customers and partners included Albertsons, Wakefern Food Corp., Woolworths Group and Chilean grocer SMU. The company filed for Chapter 11 in May 2024 and Woolworths Group acquired its micro-fulfillment assets in August 2024. Takeoff never published a public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification anywhere on its public surface, and the marketing site at www.takeoff.com no longer serves TLS. A closed API gateway at api.takeoff.com remains live and actively certificate-maintained, serving customer integrations behind authentication.

providers.name: Captain Fresh
providers.description: Captain Fresh is a Bangalore, India based B2B technology company building sustainable seafood and animal-protein supply chains worldwide, connecting fishermen, farmers, processors and retailers through a technology-enabled sourcing, cold-chain and distribution marketplace. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures, the company operates across India and international markets. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a consumer / supply-chain company profile; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found during enrichment (a marketing website only).

providers.name: Floward
providers.description: Floward is a leading online flowers and luxury gifting company headquartered in Kuwait and operating across the Middle East and the United Kingdom. Founded in 2017, the company delivers fresh flower arrangements, curated gift boxes, chocolates, cakes, and personalized gifts to more than 40 cities across 9 countries, sourcing blooms daily from ethical growers worldwide and offering same-day and scheduled delivery through its web store and mobile apps. Floward is backed by investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks Floward as a company in the network; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and corporate site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: JD Logistics
providers.description: JD Logistics (Hong Kong listed as 2618.HK) is a technology-driven supply chain and logistics service provider spun out of JD.com and backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. It operates one of China's largest integrated logistics networks, offering express and freight delivery, integrated warehouse-and-fulfillment, cold-chain and pharmaceutical logistics, cross-border shipping, oversized-item handling, and smart supply-chain technology. Through its JD Logistics Open Platform (open.jdl.com) it exposes enterprise integration services for order fulfillment, warehousing, waybill/shipment creation, tracking, and reconciliation to merchants and partners. This profile tracks the company's public developer and open-platform surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Wing
providers.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities. Wing was the first company to receive an FAA Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate for drone delivery (2019) and is an approved LAANC USS in the United States and an approved drone airspace authorization provider for CASA in Australia. Wing's commercial surface is split across two main platforms — the Wing Delivery Platform, a partner-only API and UI suite that lets retailers, restaurants, and logistics providers embed drone delivery into their own order flows (Walmart, DoorDash, Papa Johns, and others), and OpenSky, a consumer drone airspace authorization app and partner API. Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

providers.name: AVO
providers.description: Avo (avonow.com) was a New York City-based "building commerce" and workplace-amenity platform, founded 2017-2018 out of Y Combinator (S18) and backed by Insight Partners and Kleiner Perkins with roughly $84M raised. It offered white-labeled same-day delivery of groceries, household goods, alcohol and personal-care items into residential and office buildings with no order minimums or delivery fees, plus on-site and virtual event programming and corporate gifting and recognition services, serving apartment communities, corporations, hospitals and universities across New York, New Jersey, Chicago and Houston. Avo published no API, SDK or developer portal, and as of a 2026-07-20 probe its domain resolves to a parked lander with no operational hosts; Y Combinator lists the company as inactive.

providers.name: Cornershop by Uber
providers.description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.

providers.name: Fluid Truck
providers.description: Fluid Truck was a Denver, Colorado peer-to-peer commercial vehicle sharing platform founded in 2016 by James Eberhard and Jenifer Snyder, often described as "the Zipcar of commercial vehicles". It operated an app-based, self-service rental marketplace for cargo vans, box trucks and flatbeds across roughly 400 cities in 32 US states, and ran the Fluid Vehicle Investor Program (FVIP) through which individuals and small businesses bought fleets that Fluid managed and rented out. The company raised over $80 million in venture funding, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware in October 2024 after an $20.6 million cash loss in 2023, sold substantially all assets to Kingbee Rentals in December 2024, and the case converted to Chapter 7 liquidation in September 2025. The company is wound down: no developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable contract was ever published, and its own web properties no longer serve a valid TLS certificate.

providers.name: Lori Systems
providers.description: Lori Systems is a Nairobi-headquartered, pan-African digital freight platform that matches cargo owners with vetted transporters to coordinate long-haul trucking across the continent. Founded in 2016 by Josh Sandler, Jean-Claude Homawoo, and Ernest Gichini Ngaruiya, the company is now led by CEO Uche Ogboi and runs operations from offices in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, moving cargo across roughly 12 African countries with a network of 20,000+ trucks and over $10B of cargo facilitated. The platform offers shippers instant rate estimates, load matching, real-time shipment tracking, electronic proof of delivery, and integrated payments, while giving transporters access to cargo orders, truck-availability management, and prompt payment on delivery. Lori operates a public rate-card tool at ratecard.lorisystems.com, but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification; its GitHub organization is limited to small internal-tooling repositories (a Singer.io tap for Freshsales, a BambooHR Python client, a Kubernetes Terraform provider, and similar utilities) rather than a customer-facing API surface.

providers.name: Ocean Network Express
providers.description: Ocean Network Express (ONE) is a Singapore-headquartered global container liner shipping company formed in 2017 through the integration of the container shipping businesses of three Japanese carriers — Nippon Yusen Kaisha (NYK), Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), and Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K-Line) — with commercial operations launching on 1 April 2018. Operating under the magenta "ONE" brand and the Standard Carrier Alpha Code ONEY, the company runs a fleet exceeding 2,200,000 TEU across 165+ weekly service loops calling at 244+ ports worldwide, making it one of the largest ocean container carriers globally. ONE participates in THE Alliance vessel sharing agreement and offers reefer, dangerous goods, out-of-gauge, and project cargo services alongside standard dry container moves. Its customer-facing digital surface centers on the ONE eCommerce platform (ecomm.one-line.com), which provides cargo tracking, instant quotation via ONE QUOTE (powered by Descartes Kontainers), spot booking, shipping instructions, electronic bill of lading, ePayment, and demurrage/detention inquiry. A partner-facing developer portal exists at developers.one-line.com alongside EDI integration channels, but ONE does not publish a fully open, self-service OpenAPI specification, public SDK, or open-source code at either the github.com/ocean-network-express or github.com/OceanNetworkExpress organizations (both exist with zero public repositories). Tracking, booking, and schedule integrations are most commonly accessed by shippers and BCOs through third-party aggregators (Vizion, Portcast, JSONCargo, Terminal49, Tradlinx) or via DCSA-conformant carrier APIs delivered under commercial agreement.

providers.name: Salasa
providers.description: Salasa is an end-to-end eCommerce logistics provider based in Saudi Arabia, offering 3PL fulfillment (warehouse storage, automated pick/pack/ship), hyperlocal dark stores with 2-hour delivery in Riyadh, domestic on-demand and scheduled shipping, cross-border shipping with customs clearance, and reverse logistics / return management. Its Operations Management System (OMS) provides real-time tracking, inventory management, and analytics, and it connects to major eCommerce platforms (Salla, Zid, Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, Amazon, Trendyol) and offers custom API integrations for merchants automating fulfillment and order synchronization.

providers.name: Unmannd
providers.description: Unmannd (Unmannd Autonomy Pvt Ltd) is an India-based defense technology company backed by Accel and Speciale Invest, engineering autonomous drones under the banner of aerial dominance. Its TITAN 30 is an autonomous defense-logistics drone with a 30 kg max payload, 60 km/h cruise speed, 20,000 ft operational ceiling, and 30 km max range; its FURY counter-UAS interceptor was announced as launching in Q1 2026. Unmannd is a hardware/defense company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Vastera
providers.description: Vastera, Inc. was a global trade management (GTM) software and managed-services company headquartered in Dulles, Virginia. Its solutions automated the trade-management processes tied to the physical movement of goods across international borders — import/export documentation, licensing and classification, compliance and tax requirements, inventory management, and payment tracking. A Battery Ventures portfolio company, Vastera went public on Nasdaq in 2000 and was acquired by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. for $3.00 per share (approximately $129 million), effective April 1, 2005, becoming JPMorgan Chase Vastera. It no longer operates independently and publishes no public website or APIs; the vastera.com domain remains registered but is configured for email only.

providers.name: BRKZ
providers.description: BRKZ is a Saudi Arabian construction-technology company operating a B2B online marketplace for building materials and construction equipment. Positioned as a top online building materials store in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), the platform connects contractors and construction businesses with material suppliers, streamlining procurement and offering nationwide delivery across Saudi Arabia. The bilingual (Arabic and English) storefront lets buyers source construction supplies online, and the company is backed by 500 Global among its investors. This profile was enriched from BRKZ's public web presence; the company runs a private, authenticated API host (api.brkz.com) but does not publish a public developer program, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: FarMart
providers.description: FarMart is an AI-powered food sourcing and procurement platform that connects suppliers, food manufacturers, processors, and logistics providers across the global food and energy supply chain. It provides end-to-end procurement infrastructure including verified supplier discovery, five-minute AI-powered KYC verification, compliance management, market-to-factory batch traceability, automated invoicing and e-way bill generation, and real-time payment settlement in one to four hours. FarMart serves food companies, HoReCa (hospitality) buyers, and bio-fuel supply chains, with a network spanning 100+ premium buyers, 50+ food categories, and 10,000+ suppliers.

providers.name: Fox-Tech
providers.description: FOX-TECH CO. is a New Taipei City, Taiwan IoT company (founded 2016, backed by 500 Global and SparkLabs Taipei) that digitally transforms farming, logistics, cold-chain, and manufacturing operations. Its TempHawk platform pairs wireless temperature, humidity, CO2, light-intensity and soil-EC sensors over Sigfox LPWAN with web and mobile apps and cloud data analytics, helping the perishable-goods value chain monitor conditions, manage risk, and meet policy compliance. Recognized on the Forward Fooding FoodTech 500. No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Inversion Space
providers.description: Inversion Space is a Los Angeles-based aerospace and defense company founded in 2021 by Justin Fiaschetti and Austin Briggs, building autonomous, reusable, and low-cost reentry vehicles that turn space into a global logistics network. Its Arc vehicle is designed to store cargo in orbit and deliver a 500-pound payload to anywhere on Earth in under an hour, while its first spacecraft, Ray, validated key reentry subsystems. The company also develops hypersonic test capabilities and space-based interceptor technology, partnering with Anduril on the Golden Dome program and Kratos on the MACH-TB 2.0 hypersonic test program, backed by a $71M U.S. Space Force contract. It is in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: IONA
providers.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: MightyFly
providers.description: MightyFly is an autonomous air-logistics company building hybrid-electric eVTOL cargo aircraft for expedited, long-range, same-day deliveries. Its autonomous aircraft carry up to 500 pounds, travel up to 1,000 miles at roughly 150 MPH, and cut delivery emissions by around 64% versus traditional ground and air freight. MightyFly targets B2B logistics and defense delivery partnerships rather than offering a public developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or public specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Rappi
providers.description: Rappi is a Colombian-founded pan-Latin American super-app headquartered in Bogotá, with regional hubs in São Paulo and Mexico City. Founded in 2015 by Simón Borrero, Sebastián Mejía, and Felipe Villamarín, and accelerated through Y Combinator's W16 batch, Rappi operates across Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and Uruguay. The platform bundles on-demand delivery (restaurants, groceries via "Súper" and Turbo Fresh, pharmacies, retail, alcohol) with consumer fintech (RappiPay, RappiCard, RappiCash) and adjacent services such as RappiTravel and the RappiPrime subscription. Rappi's developer surface is operated through its Partners program at dev-portal.rappi.com, where approved restaurants, retailers, and middleware providers obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials to integrate with a REST API for menu and catalog management, store availability, order lifecycle events, financial reconciliation, and webhook subscriptions. Access is not self-serve — a Rappi business contact must approve onboarding, after which partners receive development-environment credentials and an integration path to production. SoftBank-backed since 2019, Rappi competes regionally with iFood, Uber Eats, and DiDi Food, with fintech ambitions overlapping Nubank, Mercado Pago, and regional neobanks.

providers.name: Zepto
providers.description: Zepto (Zepto Marketplace Private Limited) is an Indian quick-commerce grocery delivery company founded in 2021 that delivers groceries, fresh fruits and vegetables, meat, pet care, beauty and household products "in minutes" from a network of dark stores across major Indian cities. It operates a consumer-facing mobile app and website (zepto.com, formerly zeptonow.com) and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; its partner-facing surfaces are limited to merchant onboarding (Sell on Zepto / brands.zepto.co.in), delivery-partner and franchise programs. Backed by General Catalyst, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Shipium
providers.description: Shipium is a shipping platform for high-volume e-commerce, optimizing carrier selection, multi-warehouse delivery promises, and parcel routing.

providers.name: 6river
providers.description: 6 River Systems (6RS) is a warehouse fulfillment automation company founded in 2015 in Waltham, Massachusetts. Its flagship product is "Chuck," a collaborative autonomous mobile robot (AMR) that works alongside human associates to guide and optimize picking, sorting, and replenishment in distribution centers. The platform is WMS-agnostic and integrates with existing warehouse-management systems as an intelligent execution layer via a private/partner REST API for host data exchange; it does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or consumer SDKs. Norwest Venture Partners was an early investor; the company was acquired by Shopify in 2019 and by Ocado Group in 2023. The public marketing site at 6river.com currently serves a parked lander stub.

providers.name: Embark Trucks
providers.description: Embark Trucks was an autonomous-trucking company founded in 2016 and backed by Y Combinator, building a self-driving software stack (the Embark Driver) for Class 8 semi-trucks operating on interstate highway freight lanes. The company went public via a SPAC merger with Northern Star Investment Corp II in late 2021, but wound down operations in November 2023 after failing to secure additional funding; its autonomous-driving technology and engineering assets were subsequently acquired by Applied Intuition. Embark never operated a public developer platform, REST API, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile is an identity record rather than a live API. Its only surviving public technical surface is the embarktrucks GitHub organization, which hosts open-source robotics and autonomous-vehicle tooling (ROS drivers, LIDAR/camera integrations, and the webviz visualization libraries) rather than first-party API client SDKs.

providers.name: Foundation Robotics Labs
providers.description: Foundation Robotics Labs — trading publicly as Foundation and incorporated as Foundation Future Industries, Inc. — is a San Francisco humanoid robotics company founded in April 2024 by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi and Mike LeBlanc. It builds Phantom, a general-purpose humanoid robot aimed at industrial automation, logistics, inspection, disaster response and defense, and Cortex, the company's self-described physics foundation model built on Deep Variational Bayes Filters that pairs physics-informed prediction with vision-language reasoning to drive the robot. The company's published master plan runs from building humanoids through fleet coherence and on to building cities, and it states explicitly that it designs for military environments, unlike U.S. competitors committed to non-weaponization. Foundation has raised a reported $111M and is traded on the secondary market via Forge Global. As of this profile Foundation publishes NO public developer surface — no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI definition, SDK, package, MCP server or agent card. Its entire public web presence is a five-page Framer marketing site (home, Phantom, Cortex, master plan, culture, careers) with no /docs, /developers, /api, /pricing, /terms or /privacy paths and no llms.txt. Its GitHub organization (github.com/foundationbot, verified first-party by @foundation.bot commit-author domains) holds internal test benches and forks of open-source robotics tooling — Drake, jetson-containers, Kalibr, PlotJuggler, Fast-DDS, an EtherCAT master, actuator dyno benches and NXP S32K MCU demos — and contains no API specification of any kind.

providers.name: Hyster-Yale Materials Handling
providers.description: Hyster-Yale Materials Handling is a global designer, engineer, manufacturer, seller, and servicer of a comprehensive line of forklifts and aftermarket parts marketed under the Hyster and Yale brands. This repository tracks public APIs, developer resources, and integration touchpoints associated with Hyster-Yale.

providers.name: Pickle Robot Company
providers.description: Pickle Robot Company builds Physical AI robots for supply chain automation, focused on autonomously unloading non-palletized goods (floor-loaded boxes and parcels) from trucks and shipping containers at warehouse speed. Its Dill Autonomy Engine (DAE) combines classical optimal control with generative AI and machine vision so fleets improve continuously across deployments, with operational dashboards reporting picks-per-hour, unload times, and package-mix analysis. Customers include UPS and Cintas. Headquartered in the Boston, Massachusetts area, Pickle Robot is a DCVC portfolio company backed by investors including Teradyne Robotics Ventures, Toyota Ventures, Catapult Ventures, Hyperplane, and VersionOne. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK; its GitHub organization hosts robotics tooling (mostly ROS/SLAM forks) rather than API client libraries.

providers.name: Schuettflix
providers.description: Schuettflix is a German digital logistics platform for the construction industry, founded in 2018 in Guetersloh. It operates a neutral B2B marketplace that connects construction companies, bulk-material suppliers, freight forwarders and waste-disposal firms in a single fully digital workflow. Through its iOS and Android apps, customers order sand, gravel and crushed stone with transparent real-time pricing, coordinate dispatch and transport, capture delivery documentation, manage routes, and handle mineral-waste disposal and circular-economy recycling of construction materials. The company digitizes the traditionally analog and fragmented process of procuring and delivering bulk goods, earning a commission on the transactions facilitated through its platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest. No public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Schüttflix
providers.description: Schüttflix is a Gütersloh, Germany based digital logistics platform for the construction industry, describing itself as the first digital logistics hub to connect construction companies, building-material suppliers, disposal companies and carriers. The marketplace digitizes the full workflow from ordering bulk materials (sand, gravel, crushed stone) through transport dispatch to the delivery note, and adds construction-waste disposal and circular-economy recycling services. Schüttflix operates as a neutral marketplace ("we don't compete, we connect") spanning 4,000+ suppliers and disposers, 6,800+ partner carriers and 33,000+ vehicles, delivered primarily through native iOS and Android apps rather than a public API. It is a portfolio company of HV Capital, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Urban Engines
providers.description: Urban Engines was a Silicon Valley urban-mobility analytics startup founded by Shiva Shivakumar and Balaji Prabhakar that built a Space/Time Engine for analyzing how people and objects move through cities, powering commuter routing and congestion insights for cities including Washington D.C., Sao Paulo, and Singapore. Backed by a16z and GV, the company was acquired by Google in September 2016 and is now defunct; it published no public API, developer portal, or client packages, and its former website is parked on Google infrastructure.

providers.name: Jumia
providers.description: Jumia is a pan-African e-commerce company often described as the "Amazon of Africa." Headquartered in Berlin and listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker JMIA since its 2019 IPO, Jumia Technologies AG operates a third-party marketplace, a logistics network (Jumia Logistics), and a digital payments arm (JumiaPay) across eight African markets as of 2026: Egypt, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, and Uganda. The company exited Algeria in February 2026 and previously wound down Cameroon, Gabon, Rwanda, and Tunisia as part of a multi-year restructuring program targeting full-year profitability in 2027. Jumia's commerce platform connects more than 100,000 sellers with consumers across diverse categories including phones and electronics, fashion, home and living, beauty, FMCG, and groceries. Its developer surface is non-trivial: the Jumia Vendor API (vendor center, OAuth 2.0) supports order, inventory, product, and shipment integration for marketplace sellers, while the legacy SellerCenter API (a SellerCenter / Rocket Internet lineage shared with Lazada and Daraz) remains documented with PHP, Python, Ruby, and Node SDKs. JumiaPay exposes a Merchant API for payment creation, verification, refund, recurring-payment agreements, and callback-based webhooks, plus official WooCommerce and Magento payment-gateway plugins. The Jumia GitHub organization is sparse (an open-source playbook, Jumia Tech Blog, and Tech in Porto event site) while the JumiaPay AIG GitHub org hosts the WooCommerce and Magento gateway plugins under Apache 2.0.

providers.name: Radia
providers.description: Radia is a dual-use aerospace company founded in 2016 by MIT-trained aerospace engineer Mark Lundstrom, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado with a second operating base in Italy led by Giuseppe Giordo. After roughly seven years in stealth the company emerged in March 2024 with WindRunner, an aircraft it describes as the largest ever built: roughly ten times the cargo volume of a Boeing 777, sized to carry onshore wind turbine blades of up to about 105 metres, and designed to land on semi-prepared packed-dirt or gravel strips so that oversized cargo can be flown directly to a wind farm, a forward operating site or a disaster zone rather than trucked over highways it cannot fit on. Radia frames WindRunner as a deliberately low-novelty airframe assembled from existing certified technologies to shorten the certification path, targeting entry into service in the early 2030s across three markets: energy (delivering the very large blades that make low-wind onshore sites economic), defense (outsized-volume strategic airlift), and commercial supply-chain logistics. It has assembled an industrial ecosystem of more than twenty suppliers and technology partners including Aernnova, Leonardo, AFuzion, Atitech, Latecoere, Stirling Dynamics, Collier Aerospace and Maximus Air, and has raised roughly USD 128 million from investors including ConocoPhillips, Lauder Partners, LS Power Development and HCVC. Radia is an aircraft manufacturer and logistics operator rather than a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is the Strapi headless-CMS backend at radia.com/strapi that renders its own marketing site, whose content API is permission-locked and undocumented.

providers.name: 6 River Systems
providers.description: 6 River Systems is a warehouse fulfillment robotics company founded in 2015 in Waltham, Massachusetts by former Kiva Systems leaders Rylan Hamilton, Jerome Dubois, and CTO Chris Cacioppo. Its flagship product is "Chuck," a collaborative autonomous mobile robot (AMR) that works alongside human associates to guide and accelerate order picking, replenishment, and sortation in ecommerce and retail warehouses. The 6RS platform is a cloud-based execution layer that sits on top of a customer's WMS/ERP and exposes a RESTful JSON/HTTPS integration API for order, task, and operational-data exchange rather than a public self-serve developer portal. Shopify acquired 6 River Systems in 2019 for roughly $450M; Ocado Group acquired it from Shopify in May 2023, and the technology now sits within Ocado Intelligent Automation (Ocado Mobile Robot System / OMRS). Chuck has been deployed across 100-plus warehouses for 70-plus customers. Added to the API Evangelist network as a menlo-ventures portfolio lead.

providers.name: Alibaba Local Services
providers.description: Alibaba Local Services (阿里巴巴本地生活) is Alibaba Group's on-demand local-life services business, formed in 2018 by integrating the Ele.me food-delivery platform with the Koubei local-services and restaurant-discovery platform. It operates on-demand food and grocery delivery, local merchant services, reviews and reservations, and last-mile logistics across China, and received a major financing round led by the SoftBank Vision Fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the network as a lead; no distinct public developer API surface has been confirmed for the holding entity under this name (its consumer platforms Ele.me and Koubei operate their own separate open platforms).

providers.name: AllSome
providers.description: AllSome is a Malaysia-based cross-border e-commerce fulfillment, warehousing, and supply-chain company serving online marketplace sellers across Southeast Asia. It operates a fulfillment network and order-management platform that helps sellers source, store, and ship goods (notably China-to-SEA cross-border trade) across channels such as Shopee, Lazada, and TikTok Shop. AllSome is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; no public developer API surface was discoverable during enrichment (the primary website is WAF-protected and returns 403 to automated clients, and no api/developer/docs subdomains resolve).

providers.name: Axis Network Technology
providers.description: Axis (axisnet.asia) is a Malaysia-based e-commerce enabler, incorporated in 2009, providing an end-to-end managed e-commerce solution that consolidates business digitalization, inventory solutions, automated e-fulfillment, express and cross-border logistics across 98+ countries, e-commerce marketing, multi-marketplace selling, and training via Axis Academy for individuals and SMEs. It was surfaced as a portfolio lead of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Baton
providers.description: Baton is a supply-chain and logistics technology company that operates as Ryder System's Silicon Valley innovation lab following its 2022 acquisition. Founded in 2019 out of 8VC's build program, Baton originally built a network of freight "drop zones" that let long-haul truckers hand off loads for local pickup and delivery, coordinating vehicles, drop zones, warehouses, and local drivers. Today the team builds RyderShare, a collaborative logistics platform combining real-time supply-chain visibility with exception management across shipments in transit. As of this enrichment pass, baton.io publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or integration surface (the site exposes only marketing and careers pages); this profile is maintained for network discovery.

providers.name: BetaStore, Beta Store
providers.description: BetaStore (legal entity SimpleMarket Inc., trading as BetaStore.co) is a B2B retail marketplace founded in 2020 by Steve Dakayi-Kamga and Leo-Armel Tchoudjang that serves informal neighborhood retailers in West and Central Africa, operating across Nigeria, Senegal and Ivory Coast from offices in Lagos and a Wilmington, Delaware registration. The platform lets small shopkeepers restock fast-moving consumer goods directly from manufacturers and distributors at wholesale prices, ordering through SMS, chat, WhatsApp and a mobile app, with logistics partners delivering to the store within 24 hours, and it layers embedded working-capital financing on top of observed retailer sales. BetaStore raised a 2.5 million dollar pre-Series A in May 2022 led by 500 Global with VestedWorld and Loyal VC. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass BetaStore publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK or machine-readable artifact of any kind, and its betastore.co domain serves no content -- both the apex and www hosts answer every path with a blanket Cloudflare 301 to unrelated third-party domains, and no api/app/docs subdomain resolves.

providers.name: Bufferbox
providers.description: BufferBox was a Waterloo, Ontario startup that operated self-service parcel-pickup lockers for online shoppers, letting people route e-commerce deliveries to a nearby locker and collect them with a PIN. Google acquired BufferBox in November 2012 and wound the service down in early 2015. The company is defunct and operates no developer or API surface; the bufferbox.com and bufferbox.ca domains are parked (resolving to a Bizland placeholder host), so this profile carries no API artifacts. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical logistics / last-mile-delivery record.

providers.name: Burt
providers.description: Burt builds AI teammates (AI coworkers) for logistics, aimed at freight brokers and forwarders. Its agents automate the repetitive, manual work of daily freight operations — track and trace, quoting, scheduling, carrier booking, document processing, proof-of-delivery chasing, and invoice and data entry — so human operators can focus on customer relationships and growing the business. Burt gives full visibility into every AI action with human oversight and approval workflows, rolls out autonomy gradually, and learns from operator corrections and exceptions to build institutional knowledge over time. Burt is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Burt does not currently publish a public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Cargon Tech B.V.
providers.description: Cargon Tech B.V. is a supply-chain and logistics technology company backed by 500 Global. Its public presence at cargon.com positions Cargon as a fast, innovative supply-chain platform with powerful analytical tools for shippers and carriers, while the related Cargon TMS product (cargon.tech) offers a cloud transport-management system for small carriers and freight forwarders covering dispatch, fleet management, invoicing and Timocom integration. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment (the cargon.com site is a client-rendered single-page app that returns its index shell for unknown paths), so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Caviar
providers.description: Caviar is a premium restaurant food-ordering and delivery marketplace that connects diners with local, higher-end and popular restaurants for on-demand delivery and pickup. Originally launched in 2012 and later owned by Square, Caviar was acquired by DoorDash in 2019 and now operates on DoorDash's logistics and marketplace platform under the trycaviar.com brand. The service focuses on curated restaurant selection, quality-oriented ordering, courier delivery, and catering.
