Caviar does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and captures whatever public, agent-relevant surface exists.

providers.name: Con-way
providers.description: Con-way Inc. was a North American freight transportation and logistics company best known for its Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) carrier Con-way Freight along with Menlo Logistics, Con-way Truckload, and Con-way Multimodal. On October 30, 2015, XPO Logistics completed a $3 billion acquisition of Con-way; by May 2017 the Con-way brand had been fully retired in favor of XPO. This profile is preserved as a historical record; Con-way no longer operates under this name and modern shipping APIs are surfaced under XPO.

providers.name: Copia Global
providers.description: Copia Global was a Kenyan B2C e-commerce and last-mile distribution company founded by Tracey Turner and Jonathan Lewis to serve middle- and low-income consumers across rural and peri-urban Africa. Rather than a consumer website, it ran an agent-network model in which customers placed catalog orders through local agents using mobile and USSD technology, and Copia processed, aggregated, and delivered goods within days. Backed by investors including DCVC and Goodwell, the company raised a $50M Series C in 2022 to expand, but suspended Uganda operations in 2023, entered administration in May 2024, and was subsequently placed into liquidation. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or specification; its primary domain now resolves to a parked page. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead for network coverage.

providers.name: Core-Mark Holding
providers.description: Core-Mark Holding Company, a subsidiary of Performance Food Group, is one of the largest broad-line, full-service marketers and distributors of packaged consumer products to the convenience retail industry in North America. The company serves more than 41,000 retail locations across the United States and Canada, supplying tobacco, candy, snacks, beverages, foodservice, and other fast-moving consumer goods. Core-Mark provides retailer technology platforms including Core-Source Portal, Retailer Analytics, Core-Mark Ordering, and Core-Mark Intellisite.

providers.name: Deliverr
providers.description: Deliverr was an e-commerce fulfillment company founded in 2017 (Harish Abbott and Michael Krakaris) that offered fast, affordable outbound fulfillment for online sellers across marketplaces such as Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, eBay, and Wish, backed by 8vc and other investors. Shopify acquired Deliverr in 2022 and folded it into Shopify Logistics / the Shopify Fulfillment Network; in 2023 Shopify sold that logistics business to Flexport. Deliverr no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer portal or API — its former domain (deliverr.com) now redirects to flexport.com, and its fulfillment capabilities live inside Flexport's platform. This profile is retained as a historical network stub; there is no live Deliverr API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Dolly
providers.description: Dolly was a Seattle-based on-demand moving and last-mile delivery marketplace that connected people who needed help moving furniture and large items with independent "Helpers" who owned pickup trucks and vans, coordinated through consumer and retail-partner mobile apps. It grew a same-day big-and-bulky delivery network used by retailers such as IKEA, Costco, Lowe's, West Elm, and Peloton. Dolly was acquired and folded into TaskRabbit (owned by IKEA / Ingka Group); as of 2026 the dolly.com domain 301-redirects entirely to taskrabbit.com/delivery, and the service now operates under the "Taskrabbit Delivery" brand. No standalone Dolly-owned developer portal, public API, or well-known discovery surface survives — every dolly.com path redirects into TaskRabbit. This profile records the honest disposition of the company; the developer/API footprint now lives (if anywhere) under TaskRabbit, not Dolly.

providers.name: Eaze
providers.description: Eaze is a California-based cannabis marketplace and delivery platform that connects licensed dispensaries and cannabis brands with adult consumers, offering online ordering and same-day delivery of flower, edibles, vapes, and related products across the state. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in San Francisco, Eaze operates a consumer marketplace plus a technology and logistics stack for compliant retail. Backed by 500 Global and DCM Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. Eaze does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; its api.eaze.com host is an internal, bot-protected surface.

providers.name: Edfa3ly
providers.description: Edfa3ly is an Egyptian cross-border e-commerce and online shopping platform that lets consumers in Egypt and the wider MENA region buy products from international retailers and marketplaces, then handles the international shipping, customs clearance, and local delivery on their behalf. It bridges shoppers to overseas stores by managing purchasing, logistics, and payment in local currency. Edfa3ly is a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; the company does not publish a public developer program or API at this time.

providers.name: ElasticRun
providers.description: ElasticRun (legally NTEx Transportation Services Pvt Ltd) is a Pune, India based B2B e-commerce and rural logistics platform founded in 2016 by Sandeep Deshmukh, Saurabh Nigam and Shitiz Bansal. It operates an aggregated, variable-capacity transportation network that stitches together idle logistics capacity to connect FMCG brands and manufacturers to the mom-and-pop kirana stores of rural and semi-urban India. The platform blends mobile technology with local entrepreneurs to run an assisted-commerce model spanning 125,000+ kiranas and 80,000+ villages across 26 states, offering last-mile delivery, B2B distribution and supply-chain services. ElasticRun is backed by Prosus Ventures and SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile is a network stub: no public developer API, documentation or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Enjoy Technologies
providers.description: Enjoy Technology (Enjoy Technologies) was a "commerce at home" mobile-retail startup founded in 2014 by Ron Johnson, the former Apple senior vice president of retail and JCPenney CEO, and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company brought the retail store experience to customers' homes, dispatching mobile experts to deliver, set up, and demonstrate consumer electronics on behalf of partners such as carriers and device makers. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Oak Investment Partners, and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Enjoy went public via SPAC in 2021 and declared bankruptcy in 2022, with its assets subsequently acquired. Enjoy never operated a public developer program or API; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Expeditors International of Washington
providers.description: Expeditors International is a global logistics company offering freight forwarding, customs brokerage, supply chain management, warehousing, and other related logistics services. As of this update no public developer portal or openly-published APIs were located; integrations are typically delivered via private partner connectivity (EDI/B2B) and account-managed channels.

providers.name: Flirtey
providers.description: Flirtey was a drone-delivery technology company founded in 2013 by Matthew Sweeny and Tom Bass, backed by Y Combinator. It pioneered autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle delivery, conducting the first FAA-approved drone delivery in the United States in 2016 (Nevada) and running early delivery trials with partners including Domino's (the first pizza delivered by drone, in New Zealand) and 7-Eleven. Flirtey developed the Flirtey Eagle delivery drone and portable landing/loading systems aimed at medical, food, and retail last-mile logistics. The company is now defunct: it did not maintain a public developer program or API, and the flirtey.com domain has since been sold and now redirects to an unrelated business (us-stemcell.com). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fortigo
providers.description: Fortigo Network Logistics Pvt. Ltd. (4TiGO) was a Bengaluru, India technology-enabled logistics and supply-chain network platform, founded in 2015, operating an online marketplace for freight/truck transportation alongside a Digital Supply Chain Control Tower SaaS. It was backed by Accel and Nandan Nilekani's NRJN Family Trust, raising roughly $23.5M across five rounds. As of this enrichment pass the company appears deadpooled/defunct: its 4tigo.com site is unreachable (connection refused across all hosts) and no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition could be located. No API artifacts were enriched because there is no live developer surface.

providers.name: Fulfil
providers.description: Fulfil (Fulfil Solutions) is an automation company that builds robotic online-grocery fulfillment systems. Its ShopBot robots perform zero-labor pick-and-pack across all grocery temperatures and categories (ambient, refrigerated, frozen, and produce), providing item-level data and control with claimed 99% order accuracy and roughly 50% lower operating costs. The company operates automated micro-fulfillment facilities and partners with grocery and delivery operators. Backed by DCVC, Fulfil was surfaced as a portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing website but no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Full Truck Alliance
providers.description: Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd. (Manbang Group / 满帮集团, NYSE: YMM) operates a leading digital freight platform in China that connects truckers and shippers to make road transportation more efficient. It runs the Yunmanman (运满满) and Huochebang (货车帮) mobile apps, applying mobile internet, big data, and artificial intelligence to freight matching, brokerage, transaction services, and value-added offerings across hundreds of cities and tens of thousands of routes. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures, hongshan, and softbank-vision-fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or open platform on its corporate site; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: GigaCloud Technology
providers.description: GigaCloud Technology (NASDAQ: GCT) operates the GigaCloud Marketplace, a global B2B e-commerce platform for large-parcel merchandise such as furniture, home furnishings, fitness equipment, and appliances. The marketplace connects manufacturers, primarily in Asia, with resellers across the United States, Europe, and Japan, integrating product discovery, transactions, and end-to-end cross-border logistics including ocean freight, warehousing, and last-mile delivery. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a dcm-ventures portfolio lead. Enrichment probes found no public developer portal, API documentation, or well-known discovery surface; the corporate site is behind bot protection (HTTP 403), so this profile is limited to verified domain-security posture and company identity.

providers.name: GLP
providers.description: GLP is a leading global logistics real estate and investment management company, developing and operating warehouses, distribution centers, and supply-chain infrastructure alongside a large fund and asset-management business. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of hillhouse and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Sector: logistics. As of this enrichment pass GLP publishes a WAF-protected corporate website but no discoverable public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal; this profile remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Haven
providers.description: Haven, Inc. was an ocean freight technology company founded in 2014 that built software to automate quoting, booking, document management, and shipment management for commodity producers, traders, and freight forwarders moving international ocean cargo. Backed by DCVC, Haven was acquired by supply-chain visibility platform FourKites in April 2021, and its technology became the foundation of FourKites' Dynamic Ocean product for end-to-end international ocean shipment visibility. Haven no longer operates an independent public developer program or API; the Haven brand survives only as the "Haven Marketplace" login at app.haveninc.com, now operated as part of FourKites.

providers.name: High Jump Software
providers.description: HighJump Software was a Minneapolis-based provider of supply chain execution software, best known for its warehouse management system (WMS) and its extensible, configurable architecture for distribution, direct-store-delivery, and manufacturing operations. The company was acquired by Battery Ventures in 2014, expanded through acquisitions (Accellos, Nexus, TrueCommerce lines), then acquired by Körber in 2017 and folded into Körber Supply Chain Software. As of 2024 the portfolio was rebranded Infios. The standalone HighJump brand is retired: highjump.com now 301-redirects to infios.com, and the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification. This profile is retained as a historical / acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hop Aero
providers.description: Hop Aero is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) aerospace and defense company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2024 by Jacob Balaj and Matija Milenovic. The company develops hypersonic rocket cargo vehicles that deliver payloads point-to-point into austere, contested environments hundreds of miles away in minutes, aiming to give the United States and its allies an asymmetric logistics advantage. Hop Aero has raised a $3M pre-seed round and won a $1.25M U.S. Air Force SBIR award; its team draws on experience from SpaceX, Virgin Orbit, Masten Space Systems, SpinLaunch, and Destinus. This is a hardware-stage company with no public API or developer surface at the time of profiling; this record was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and is maintained for network discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Inloop Robotics
providers.description: Inloop Robotics (InLoop) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup in San Francisco offering robotics-as-a-service for warehouses, fulfillment centers, and light manufacturing. Its bimanual "Loop V1" robot performs box assembly, kitting, visual inspection, content preparation, unpackaging, and order pick-and-pack. The system runs a hybrid-autonomy, human-in-the-loop model: onboard AI handles routine work while remote teleoperators take over on edge cases, and production failures feed continuous learning. InLoop sells this as a flat monthly subscription that bundles the hardware, ongoing AI updates, and 24/7 teleassistance fallback, rather than selling robots outright. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site only, with no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending any future developer/API program.

providers.name: J&T Express
providers.description: J&T Express (J&T Global Express Ltd, HKEX: 1519) is a global logistics service operator whose core business is express parcel delivery and international logistics. Founded in Indonesia in 2015, it operates express delivery networks across 13 countries including Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Cambodia, Singapore, China, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Mexico, Brazil, and Egypt, with international freight services reaching Asia, Europe, Africa, the Americas, and Oceania. The company serves e-commerce sellers and consumers with parcel pickup, sorting, line-haul, last-mile delivery, and track-and-trace. As of this profile J&T Express publishes a public track-and-trace web experience and regional merchant onboarding, but no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: JD Business
providers.description: JD Business is the enterprise-facing arm of JD.com (Jingdong), one of China's largest technology and retail companies, offering B2B procurement, supply-chain, and corporate purchasing services to businesses. JD.com operates across retail, logistics, technology, health, and industrials, and runs the JD Open Platform (JOS / "Zeus" Developer Center) at jos.jd.com, where third-party merchants and partners integrate with JD's e-commerce, order, product, and logistics systems. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and is being enriched from JD's public surface; JD's developer platform and enterprise services are primarily China-market and Chinese-language.

providers.name: Khazenly
providers.description: Khazenly is a Cairo, Egypt based cloud order-fulfillment and e-commerce enablement platform that helps online merchants and brands manage the full post-checkout journey. Its stack combines an order management system, warehousing and pick-pack-ship fulfillment, last-mile delivery, and cash-on-delivery collection so sellers can outsource operations while retaining visibility. Khazenly connects to popular e-commerce storefronts and marketplaces to sync orders, inventory, and shipping status. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network; its public developer/API surface is not openly documented, so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signals rather than harvested API artifacts.

providers.name: Kyte
providers.description: Kyte was a full-stack technology-operations company that delivered rental cars on demand to the customer's door, positioning itself for any trip longer than a rideshare — a car for a day, a few days, or longer — with no rental counters, no lines and no paperwork. Headquartered in San Francisco, the company combined a consumer mobile and web booking experience with its own fleet and delivery operations ("bits and atoms"), and at its peak operated in 14 US markets delivering tens of thousands of trips per month. It was a growth-stage portfolio company of Anthemis under that firm's Data, Tech and Infrastructure thesis. Kyte was a consumer-facing operator and never published a public developer program, API, SDK or developer portal, and as of this enrichment pass its web properties no longer serve the company.

providers.name: makespace
providers.description: makespace was a New York-founded, full-service consumer storage company (professional pickup, packing, digital photo cataloging, and on-demand redelivery) added to the API Evangelist network as a slow-ventures portfolio-lead stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the makespace.com domain 301-redirects to clutter.com, the storage brand now operated as Clutter by Iron Mountain, and the company exposes no public developer program, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or documented API surface. This profile records the honest result of the pipeline: identity plus a live domain-security probe, with no API artifacts available to harvest.

providers.name: Markato
providers.description: Markato (legally On Your Marks) is a brand builder and distributor for health, beauty, and wellness brands across Asia, positioning itself as a next-generation distribution disruptor. From bases in Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, Thailand, and Australia, it helps high-potential brands enter, grow, and dominate the region's most competitive markets. Its capabilities span strategic channel development into top-tier offline and online retailers (Sephora, Watsons, Mannings, SaSa), e-commerce and social commerce operations across Shopee, TikTok, and Lazada, 360-degree marketing and brand building, and end-to-end local operations, logistics, product registration, and compliance. Markato is backed by a roughly US$4M seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with a team drawn from L'Oreal, P&G, McKinsey, and Lane Crawford. Markato is a services and distribution business and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Milk Moovement
providers.description: Milk Moovement is a dairy supply chain software company that provides cloud-based logistics, scheduling, routing, quality tracking, and automated payroll tools for dairy cooperatives and processors across North America. The platform digitizes the movement of milk from farm to processor, giving producers, haulers, and cooperatives real-time visibility into the dairy supply chain. The company was surfaced via the techstars portfolio and enriched into the API Evangelist network; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or status page.

providers.name: myBOX
providers.description: myBOX was an on-demand self-storage service founded in 2015 in Seoul, South Korea, and backed by 500 Global. It delivered storage boxes to a user's door for storing unused luggage and goods, offering free pickup and a range of container sizes for documents, clothes, and bulky items. The company has since permanently closed; its site (my-box.kr) no longer resolves and it exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical surface. Retained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead; no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: Nistevo
providers.description: Nistevo was a Collaborative Logistics Network — a web-based, on-demand (ASP/SaaS) transportation management platform that let manufacturers, retailers, and carriers plan, tender, execute, and settle inbound and outbound truckload freight collaboratively. Founded in 1996 in Eden Prairie, Minnesota (originally TransView Corporation) and backed by Insight Partners, it served shippers such as General Mills, Land O'Lakes, Georgia-Pacific, Cargill, and Baxter, and was acquired by Sterling Commerce (an AT&T subsidiary) in May 2006. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; nistevo.com is parked and serves no live web application.

providers.name: Nizthewiz
providers.description: NizTheWiz Technology Sdn Bhd is a Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia based logistics startup founded in 2015 that operates a crowd-sourced, on-demand same-day local courier and delivery platform. Its consumer mobile app connects senders with a crowd-sourced fleet of couriers and provides live GPS tracking and full last-mile transparency across the delivery lifecycle. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NizTheWiz publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs — its product is a consumer-facing courier app rather than a developer platform, so there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Outrider
providers.description: Outrider is an autonomous yard technology company that automates distribution yard operations with self-driving, all-electric yard trucks (hostlers). The Outrider System combines autonomous driving software, robotics for connecting and disconnecting trailers, and site operations software to move trailers between docks, parking spots, and staging lanes in large logistics yards. Headquartered in Golden, Colorado, Outrider targets shippers and logistics operators seeking to improve safety, sustainability, and throughput in the supply chain. The company is backed by investors including 8VC. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been identified for Outrider.

providers.name: Packfleet
providers.description: Packfleet was an all-electric last-mile parcel courier based in London, delivering for hundreds of merchant customers using a zero-emission electric-van fleet with a focus on sustainable, reliable next-day delivery. Backed by Creandum as a venture-funded climate-logistics company, Packfleet wound down its independent brand in March 2025, with its deliveries transitioned to DHL. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was ever published; this profile is retained as a network record. Enriched: no API surface (company now operates as DHL).

providers.name: PCH International
providers.description: PCH International (pchintl.com) is a global supply chain solutions provider that helps brands bring innovative physical products to market across the entire product lifecycle. Its services span new product introduction (NPI) planning, design and development, validation and manufacturing (EVT/DVT/PVT), and post-production revenue optimization, plus global logistics, direct-to-consumer (D2C) transformation, supply-chain financing, and sustainability programs. PCH serves personal care and beauty, health and fitness, home and lifestyle, accessories, audio and entertainment, and smart retail sectors. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners, PCH is a B2B services provider with no public developer API or platform at this time.

providers.name: Penske
providers.description: A diversified transportation services conglomerate operating truck leasing, logistics, automotive retail, and professional motorsports across North America. Penske Corporation spans Penske Truck Leasing (full-service leasing, rental, and contract maintenance), Penske Logistics (supply chain management, warehousing, distribution, dedicated contract carriage), Penske Automotive Group (retail automotive dealerships in the US, UK, Germany, Italy, Japan, Australia, and New Zealand), and Team Penske (motorsports). The corporate parent has 73,000+ employees and approximately $43B+ in consolidated revenue. Customer self-service is delivered through web and mobile portals (Penske Fleet Insight, Penske Truck Leasing app, Penske Truck Rental); Penske does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal. Penske Automotive Group is the publicly traded subsidiary (NYSE - PAG).

providers.name: Phantom Auto
providers.description: Phantom Auto was a Mountain View, California and Ra'anana, Israel teleoperation company founded in 2017 by Shai Magzimof (CEO) and Elliot Katz (CBO) that built a remote-driving and remote-operation platform letting a human operator monitor and drive a vehicle from thousands of miles away over bonded commercial cellular links. It launched aimed at robotaxis and self-driving trucks as a safety fallback for autonomous vehicles, then pivoted in 2019 to logistics — remotely operated forklifts and yard trucks that have no autonomy of their own, plus autonomous sidewalk delivery robots — and signed customers including Maersk, CJ Logistics, ArcBest and Serve Robotics. It raised roughly $95M in total from Bessemer Venture Partners, Maniv Mobility, InfraBridge and strategic investors ArcBest and ConGlobal, closing a $25M round in 2023, and acquired Swedish low-latency video streaming company Voysys AB in October 2022. Phantom Auto ceased operations on 12 March 2024 after a funding round fell through, laying off its roughly 100-120 remaining employees. The company published no developer portal, public API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP manifest or agent card) while it operated, and its primary host phantom.auto no longer resolves in DNS at all. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: QikPod
providers.description: QikPod was an Accel-backed Indian startup that built an automated parcel locker network for last-mile e-commerce delivery, letting shoppers collect and return packages from unattended smart lockers placed in apartments, offices, and retail locations. The company has since rebranded and pivoted to Leapmile Robotics, a nano-warehouse automation and intelligent fulfillment platform that uses robotics to handle storage, retrieval, picking, auditing, and dispatch inside compact autonomous warehouse facilities. The legacy qikpod.com domain now redirects to leapmile.com/qikpod. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public developer API surface has been found for either the QikPod or Leapmile properties.

providers.name: Quickshipper
providers.description: QuickShipper is a last-mile delivery and fleet management SaaS platform that helps businesses manage order fulfillment and deliveries. It provides route optimization, order batching, automated or manual dispatching, a courier mobile app, real-time tracking, branded customer notifications, and business analytics. Companies can operate their own fleet or connect with third-party courier providers, and can sync orders automatically through API integration and WooCommerce/WordPress plugins. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: RedCap
providers.description: RedCap is an automotive dealer service software company that built an on-demand vehicle pickup-and-delivery, loaner, and shuttle platform for dealership fixed-operations (service) departments — offering live vehicle tracking, automated dispatching, at-home loaner contracting, on-demand parts fulfillment, and Uber-integrated shuttle coordination that plug into a dealership's existing DMS and service tools. Backed by Uncork Capital, RedCap was acquired by Solera and is now operated as Solera Service Suite; its former site (getredcap.com) redirects to the Solera Service Suite product. RedCap does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: RiskPulse
providers.description: RiskPulse was a supply chain risk and weather-intelligence company (also known by its Stormpulse brand) that scored and forecast weather, transit, and logistics disruption risk across supply chain networks. It was acquired by Everstream Analytics; the riskpulse.com and stormpulse.com domains now 301-redirect to everstream.ai, where the capability lives on as Everstream's Weather Intelligence and Analytics product. As of this enrichment pass there is no standalone RiskPulse public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface, and Everstream exposes no public API either. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company lead.

providers.name: Rockport Trade Systems
providers.description: Rockport Trade Systems is a global trade management (GTM) software company providing customs compliance, import and export management, and trade-content solutions to enterprises. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners, it was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company operates a corporate marketing website but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface, and the site actively blocks automated access (HTTP 403), so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Ruedata
providers.description: Ruedata (RueData AI) is an AI predictive tire-management software platform for commercial fleet operators. It combines a smart digital inspection app, the TLGX precision tire-measurement device (tread depth to +/-1/32nd and pressure to +/-0.25 percent), and a centralized web platform to help fleets prevent tire blowouts, cut maintenance costs, extend tire lifecycle, and improve road safety. Its business-intelligence layer applies predictive analytics for tire wear and route optimization, and it integrates with major telematics providers such as Samsara, Geotab, Netfleet, and Traffilog plus ERP systems via direct API connections. Ruedata is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Servo7
providers.description: Servo7 is a Y Combinator-backed warehouse robotics company that builds AI-powered robots for automating physical material-handling tasks such as loose-loaded container unloading, mixed-pallet palletizing, depalletizing, sortation, and case handling (up to a 20kg payload). Its differentiator is a no-code, demonstration-based deployment model in which an operator shows the robot the task to automate, with no engineers or integration project and no facility redesign required. Servo7 works with logistics providers including CEVA, Stord, DHL, and PostNL. It is a physical-robotics/hardware company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Skipthedishes
providers.description: SkipTheDishes is a Canadian online food-delivery marketplace headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, founded in 2012 and acquired by Just Eat (now Just Eat Takeaway.com) in 2016, under which it operates as the group's Canadian brand. It connects diners with local restaurants and a network of independent couriers for on-demand food delivery and pickup across Canadian cities via its consumer website and mobile apps, and runs a restaurant partner onboarding program and a courier (Skip Network) program. As of this enrichment pass SkipTheDishes publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. The primary domain is served behind Cloudflare bot protection and the partner/partners subdomains are static marketing/onboarding pages, so no OpenAPI, webhook, or SDK surface is available to harvest.

providers.name: Stratim
providers.description: Stratim (originally incorporated as Zirx in 2014, rebranded to Stratim in 2017) was a San Francisco-based SaaS company that built an enterprise fleet-operations and logistics platform for transportation companies, autonomous-vehicle operators, and urban fleets. Its three product lines were the Stratim Platform (fleet operations software), the Stratim Exchange (on-the-ground vendor fulfillment), and the Stratim Marketplace (fleet-owner/vendor transactions), and it advertised API access, a workforce app, processing-engine integration, and SMS updates. Founded by Shmulik Fishman and Sean Behr and backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures ($36.4M raised), Stratim was acquired by ACV Auctions in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the stratim.com domain is held in custodial parking (CSC Corporate Domains) with no live website, developer portal, documentation, or reachable API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: SynQuest
providers.description: SynQuest, Inc. (formerly Nasdaq: SYNQ) was an Atlanta, Georgia based supply-chain planning and logistics software company that provided e-business solutions to optimize the financial and operational performance of the supply chain, including transportation, distribution, and inventory planning and simulation for customers such as Ford Motor Company. SynQuest reverse-merged with Viewlocity, Inc. in November 2002 (Viewlocity merged into SynQuest as the surviving entity) and was delisted from the Nasdaq SmallCap Market shortly after. Insight Partners (formerly Insight Venture Partners) was an early investor, which is why the company appears in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. The company is inactive today and publishes no live website, developer portal, or public API surface; enrichment searches found only historical SEC filings and press coverage.

providers.name: Trinity Industries
providers.description: Trinity Industries, Inc. is a leading manufacturer and lessor of railcars in North America, providing products and services to the industrial, energy, transportation, and construction sectors. The company designs, manufactures, leases, and manages railcars used to transport commodities such as energy products, agricultural goods, construction materials, and consumer staples. Trinity operates a lease fleet of over 140,000 owned and managed railcars through its TrinityRail division.

providers.name: Vision Space Inc.
providers.description: Vision Space Inc. (VisionSpace) is a South Korean company building Physical AI robot simulation software for automation in the logistics and manufacturing sectors. Its TESSERACT product implements logistics and manufacturing sites as digital twins, visualizing process data and predicting operational efficiency through AI-based simulation, while its TARS product delivers real-time 3D monitoring that integrates and manages data from equipment and robots in a unified 3D control dashboard. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass VisionSpace publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Weft
providers.description: Weft was a Burlington, Vermont based supply-chain logistics startup, founded by Marc Held around 2013-2014, that combined hardware sensors and software to track the shipping of physical goods worldwide in real time. It raised a seed round of under $1M led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Data Elite, with plans for a $5M Series A. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct: no live corporate website, no developer portal, and no public API surface could be found. Candidate domains were probed and none host an active product (weft.com refused connection, weft.io does not resolve, weft.ai is a parked domain listed for sale).

providers.name: XELUS
providers.description: Xelus was a service parts planning and optimization software company founded in 1972 and headquartered in Fairport, New York, providing inventory management and supply chain solutions for the telecommunications, aerospace and defense, and high-tech industries. An Insight Venture Partners portfolio company, Xelus was acquired by Click Commerce on May 27, 2005, and no longer operates independently. Its website (xelus.com) is defunct and the company publishes no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or packages.

providers.name: Yetcargo
providers.description: Yetcargo is a Mexican freight and cargo transportation company that connects businesses needing to move goods with a network of reliable carriers, handling both local and long-distance (foráneo) shipments. Operating a Spanish-language web platform, it positions itself as a trusted cargo-transport provider ("Tu proveedor confiable de transporte de carga") for shippers who need to resolve local and out-of-town delivery problems. Yetcargo was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Zapp
providers.description: Zapp is a London-based premium quick-commerce (q-commerce) business that delivers daily essentials such as snacks, drinks, groceries, household items and pharmacy needs across central London in minutes, 24/7. Founded in 2020 by Navid Hadzaad and Joe Falter, the company operates a network of micro-fulfilment "dark stores" and a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) rather than a public developer platform. Zapp is a venture-backed company whose investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this profile, Zapp exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; it is a business-to-consumer delivery brand surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: COSCO Shipping
providers.description: A Chinese state-owned multinational shipping and logistics conglomerate and the world's largest container shipping fleet by capacity. Operates container shipping, port terminals, bulk cargo services, and digital supply chain platforms (Syncon Hub, My Reefer, Hi-Dolphin) across global trade routes.

providers.name: CaaStle
providers.description: CaaStle Inc. was a New York based business-to-business "Clothing-as-a-Service" company that built white-label clothing rental, subscription and resale infrastructure for apparel retailers, operating tenant-branded storefronts and reverse-logistics for partner brands rather than selling directly to consumers. The company collapsed in 2025: its board confirmed financial distress and furloughed staff in April 2025, and it filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware on 20 June 2025 (case 25-11187), electing liquidation over reorganization. Founder and chief executive Christine Hunsicker resigned amid allegations of fabricated financial disclosures and later pleaded guilty to a fraud scheme prosecutors valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars. CaaStle never operated a public developer program, and the caastle.com domain has since passed out of the company's control.

providers.name: Dunzo
providers.description: Dunzo was an Indian hyperlocal delivery and quick-commerce platform founded in July 2014 in Bengaluru by Kabeer Biswas, Ankur Agarwal, Dalvir Suri and Mukund Jha, which grew from a WhatsApp group into an app-based service delivering groceries, food, medicines, pet supplies and same-city packages across up to nine Indian cities. Its Dunzo for Business (D4B) offering gave merchants last-mile delivery through a partner API and through multi-carrier aggregators. Backed by Google, Blume Ventures, Alteria Capital and Reliance Retail, the company was dissolved on 14 January 2025; the app and website were shut down and every Dunzo-operated host, including its merchant API, is now offline. This profile is retained as a historical record — Dunzo publishes no developer portal, documentation, specification or support channel today.

providers.name: Inxeption
providers.description: Inxeption was a B2B "industrial commerce" software company founded in 2017 by serial entrepreneur Farzad Dibachi and headquartered in Silicon Valley (San Jose / Cupertino, California). It sold a cloud commerce platform that let manufacturers, distributors and wholesalers stand up a branded online storefront and digital product catalog, then manage quoting, contract-specific pricing, purchase orders, bulk and multimodal orders, freight and logistics, returns, payments and sales analytics from one place — a category it marketed as the "Industrial Commerce SuperApp". Its best-known product was Inxeption Zippy, launched in March 2019 with UPS after an equity investment from the UPS Strategic Enterprise Fund, which bundled UPS as the shipper of choice into the storefront. The company raised roughly $186M across its rounds, including a $125M Series E in January 2022. Inxeption shut down on 2024-08-15. It never operated a public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK or package was ever published, and its integration story was bespoke customer and EDI connections delivered under contract. Today only the apex domain resolves, and it no longer belongs to the company — it is listed for sale on the serp.domains domain marketplace. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Landstar System
providers.description: Landstar System is a worldwide, asset-light provider of integrated transportation management solutions delivering safe, specialized transportation services to a broad range of customers.

providers.name: ShipEngine
providers.description: ShipEngine (an Auctane / ShipStation company) is a shipping API for rate shopping, label generation, tracking, and address validation across major carriers.

providers.name: Transfix
providers.description: Transfix is a New York-based freight technology company that, since divesting its brokerage operation to NFI Industries in June 2024, operates as a SaaS and data company providing AI-powered Transportation Management System (TMS) software to freight brokers, third-party logistics providers (3PLs), shippers, and carriers across the United States. The Transfix TMS unifies pricing, planning, execution, and billing in a single platform, with feature areas covering Smart Pricing and Quoting, RFP Management and Collaboration, Coverage and Carrier Management, Streamlined Scheduling, Operations and Automation, Invoicing and Payments, and Reporting and Insights. Core AI capabilities include the Custom Rate Prediction Suite for spot and contract pricing across Dry Van, Reefer, and Flatbed equipment, and the RFP Workflow with a Smart Upload feature that structures bid data from heterogeneous file formats. Transfix markets integrations with existing TMS, carrier networks, and data sources, and references freight API integrations in marketing material, but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or open-source repositories. NFI Industries is the platform's anchor third-party customer following the brokerage divestiture.

providers.name: Owens & Minor
providers.description: Owens & Minor is a global Fortune 500 healthcare solutions company providing essential products and services to healthcare providers and manufacturers across the continuum of care, including medical and surgical supplies distribution, home healthcare equipment (Apria, Byram Healthcare), and outsourced logistics. No public APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories
providers.description: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories (RedWing Labs, operated by Kitemaps AMS Pvt Ltd) is a Bangalore, India based, Techstars-backed company that designs, develops and deploys fully autonomous drones to transform logistics supply chains. It offers a fleet of long-range, urban and medium-range delivery aircraft plus an operations software suite, and runs an autonomous four-step delivery flow (order, handoff to flight operations, proof of delivery, return to hub) used to move healthcare products, food and other goods within the hour. The company reports operational milestones including 145,930+ kilometers flown and thousands of deliveries completed. RedWing does not publish a first-party developer API; its public agent surface is the platform-provided Wix Site MCP endpoint advertised in its llms.txt.

providers.name: Jabil
providers.description: Jabil is a global manufacturing services company that provides engineering, supply chain, and manufactured product solutions for the world's leading brands across industries including automotive, healthcare, industrial, consumer electronics, networking, and cloud infrastructure.

providers.name: Bykea
providers.description: Bykea is a Karachi-based Pakistani mobility and logistics super-app that offers app-hailed motorbike rides, on-demand parcel and food delivery, cash pickup and drop-off, and digital payments across major Pakistani cities. It connects a large network of motorbike captains with riders and merchants, positioning itself as a low-cost transport, last-mile logistics, and financial services platform for the mass market. Backed by Prosus Ventures (Naspers), Bykea was added to the API Evangelist network as a mobility-sector portfolio lead; this profile has been enriched with the provider's public security surface (a live RFC 9116 security.txt and a HackerOne bug bounty program) and domain-security posture. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or partner API documentation is exposed - the primary web surface sits behind Cloudflare bot protection.

providers.name: MAYD
providers.description: MAYD (Meds At Your Doorstep) is a Berlin-based on-demand medication delivery service building a digital healthcare platform for Europe. Founded in 2021 by Hanno Heintzenberg and Lukas Pieczonka (previously McMakler), MAYD partners with local pharmacies to deliver over-the-counter and prescription medications to consumers' doors in about 30 minutes, 365 days a year, across German cities including Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Frankfurt, Cologne and Düsseldorf. The company operates a consumer mobile app and website (getmayd.com) and raised a ~EUR 30M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners in January 2022, with participation from Target Global, 468 Capital and Earlybird Venture Capital. MAYD is a consumer-facing (B2C) delivery business and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface; it is a Stripe payments customer for its checkout and billing.

providers.name: Gallatin AI
providers.description: Gallatin AI builds AI-powered software for defense logistics, giving military planners and logisticians decision advantage across the tactical, operational, and strategic levels of the supply chain. Its products include Navigator, an AI decision-support "S4" that aggregates and analyzes brigade-level logistics reports in real time to streamline resupply planning; Burrow, a DoD-compliant third-party logistics (3PL) solution managing vendor qualification, transportation, inventory, storage, and fulfillment for domestic and international operations; and Phalanx, an automated asset and in-transit visibility system combining traditional reporting with hardware sensors and computer vision. Founded by veterans of Scale AI, Palantir, Amazon Prime Air, and the DoD, the company emerged from stealth in 2025 and is backed by 8VC, Silent Ventures, Timeless, Moonshots Capital, and Banter Capital.

providers.name: Performance Food Group
providers.description: Performance Food Group is one of the largest foodservice distributors in North America, marketing and distributing food and food-related products to independent and chain restaurants and other institutional customers.

providers.name: RXO
providers.description: RXO is a freight and logistics platform that connects shippers and carriers across truckload, less-than-truckload, managed transportation, and last-mile delivery. The company operates RXO Connect, a digital freight platform that uses machine learning and AI across a network of approximately 150,000 independent carriers. RXO does not currently publish a public developer API portal on its corporate website.

providers.name: Phillips 66
providers.description: Phillips 66 is a diversified energy manufacturing and logistics company with midstream, chemicals, refining, and marketing and specialties businesses. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for Phillips 66.

providers.name: GoTo
providers.description: GoTo (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, IDX: GOTO) is the largest technology group in Indonesia, formed in May 2021 through the merger of the on-demand and ride-hailing pioneer Gojek and the e-commerce marketplace Tokopedia. GoTo operates a super-app ecosystem spanning on-demand services (ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, logistics), e-commerce, and financial technology through GoTo Financial (including GoPay, one of Indonesia's leading digital wallets). The group serves Indonesia's population of more than 270 million, connecting tens of millions of consumers with millions of merchants and driver-partners, and is estimated to contribute roughly 2 percent of Indonesia's GDP. GoTo is backed by a roster of blue-chip investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Alibaba, Google, Tencent, Temasek, and Sequoia Capital India. This company profile was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. Note that GoTo Group's developer surfaces are published per product (Gojek/GoBiz, Tokopedia, GoTo Financial/Midtrans) rather than at a single group-level developer portal; this record profiles the parent holding company.

providers.name: Adams Resources & Energy
providers.description: Adams Resources & Energy is a diversified energy company engaged in the marketing, transportation, terminalling, and storage of crude oil and other related petroleum products in select markets across the United States. Through its subsidiaries GulfMark Energy, Firebird Bulk Carriers, Phoenix Oil, and Victoria Express Pipeline, the company purchases approximately 90,000 barrels per day at the wellhead and operates over 260 tractor-trailers and 112 pipeline inventory locations. Adams Resources & Energy serves multiple U.S. petroleum basins including the Gulf Coast, Eagle Ford Shale, Permian Basin, Bakken Shale, and Michigan, with over $1 billion in annual revenues and 400+ employees.

providers.name: DeepWay 深向
providers.description: DeepWay (深向科技 / Shenxiang Technology) is a Chinese intelligent new-energy heavy-truck company, backed by Baidu and Qiming Venture Partners, that designs and manufactures electric autonomous freight trucks it calls RoboTrucks. Its vehicle line includes the Xingchen II (深向星辰 II) and Xingtu (深向星途) electric heavy trucks paired with the Tianji (天玑) driver-assistance and autonomous driving stack, an AI-based fleet management platform, and a vehicle-owner mobile app. DeepWay reports 7,500+ activated L2 vehicles, a 30%+ subscription rate, and 300M+ km of assisted-driving operation, and follows a roadmap from L2 assistance (2023) to L4 platooning (2025) to single-vehicle L4 autonomy (2028). Its business model progresses from vehicle sales to subscription services to large-scale autonomous logistics capacity. As of this enrichment pass DeepWay publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification — this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: dstzc
providers.description: dstzc (地上铁, DiShangTie Green Technology, Shenzhen) is a leading Chinese provider of digitalized operations-management solutions for new-energy (electric) logistics vehicles. It operates a full-lifecycle fleet platform covering vehicle sales and leasing, digital fleet management, safety and risk management, maintenance, charging and battery-swap services, and residual-value management, reporting 224,000+ operational vehicles across 3,246 service locations spanning all 333 prefecture-level regions of mainland China. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company has no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained as a company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: firstgrid
providers.description: The domain firstgrid.cn resolves to Shanghai Shouige Network Technology Co., Ltd. (上海首格网络科技有限公司 / "Shouige Network"), a Chinese software and logistics-services provider focused on the medical-device industry. Its products include the Medical Jiecloud Platform (医捷云), a bidirectional logistics intelligence and supply-chain management system, a public database platform, and third-party warehousing/distribution services for medical-device producers, distributors, and 3PLs, with offices in Shanghai and an R&D center in Hangzhou. The company was surfaced as a portfolio lead of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the public site is a Chinese-language corporate marketing site and exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested. Note: the recorded English name "firstgrid" is the pinyin of 首格 (Shǒugé) and the domain/company identity should be verified against the intended qiming portfolio company.

providers.name: Lansing Trade Group
providers.description: Lansing Trade Group was an international merchandiser, marketer, and logistics company specializing in bulk commodities including grains, biofuels, and energy products. In 2022, The Andersons completed the acquisition of Lansing Trade Group; its commodities business now operates as part of The Andersons' Trade Group.

providers.name: Par Pacific Holdings
providers.description: Par Pacific Holdings is an entrepreneurial liquid fuels company focused on owning and operating energy and infrastructure businesses in logistically- complex markets. The company operates refining, retail, and logistics businesses across Hawaii, Washington, Wyoming, and Montana, with retail brands including 76, Hele, and nomnom.

providers.name: PBF Energy
providers.description: PBF Energy is one of the largest independent petroleum refiners and suppliers of unbranded transportation fuels, heating oils, lubricants, petrochemical feedstocks, and other petroleum products in the United States, operating refineries and a logistics network across the country.

providers.name: Trella
providers.description: Trella is a Cairo-headquartered B2B trucking marketplace and digital freight platform that connects shippers with carriers across the Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan (MENA-P). Founded in 2019 by Omar Hagrass, Ali El Atrash, and Pierre Saad and backed by Y Combinator, Trella runs a digital load marketplace, a carrier mobile app, and a shipper web dashboard that together replace the traditional broker-driven, paper-based long-haul trucking workflow. Core platform services include load posting and carrier matching, instant quoting, GPS tracking and live shipment visibility, electronic proof of delivery (ePODs), load insurance, a control-tower operations layer for carrier quality and performance, and integrated payments and invoicing between shippers and carriers. The network spans 30,000+ carriers and operates from major freight hubs including Cairo, Alexandria, Port Said, Damietta, Sokhna, Jeddah, Dammam, Riyadh, and Dubai, serving industries such as FMCG, construction, manufacturing, agriculture, mining, e-commerce, retail, electronics, ceramics, and freight forwarding. Trella's revenue model is marketplace take-rate and value-added logistics services; there is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks catalog, or open-source platform release for the Trella marketplace.

providers.name: GXO Logistics
providers.description: GXO Logistics is a leading global provider of pure-play contract logistics, offering warehousing, distribution, e-commerce fulfillment, supply chain optimization, and reverse logistics services.

providers.name: Kobo360
providers.description: Kobo360 is a Nigerian-founded, pan-African B2B digital freight marketplace and logistics technology platform headquartered in Lagos, with operations across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Togo, Uganda, and other African countries. Founded in 2017 by Obi Ozor and Ife Oyedele II, Kobo360 operates an "Uber for trucks" long-haul logistics model that matches cargo owners and enterprise shippers with truck owners and drivers through a single digital ecosystem. The company runs the Global Logistics Operating System (G-LOS), an enterprise-grade logistics SaaS / digital freight forwarding platform that provides shipper dashboards, end-to-end shipment visibility, driver and truck ratings, embedded credit and working-capital products for carriers, and route and load optimization across the Kobo network of registered drivers and trucks. Kobo360 serves large FMCG, manufacturing, and commodities customers including Dangote, DHL, Honeywell, Olam, and Unilever, and has raised funding from investors such as Goldman Sachs, IFC, TLcom Capital, and Western Asset. Kobo360 does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open developer portal; integrations with shippers and partners are delivered through enterprise onboarding rather than a self-service API program.

providers.name: Universal Hydrogen
providers.description: Universal Hydrogen Co. was a Hawthorne, California hydrogen-aviation startup founded in 2020 by former Airbus CTO Paul Eremenko to decarbonize regional air travel. Rather than building a hydrogen pipeline network, it proposed a modular capsule model: lightweight hydrogen capsules loaded into aircraft with existing cargo handling equipment, paired with fuel-cell powertrain conversion kits for regional turboprops such as the ATR 72 and De Havilland Dash 8. In March 2023 it flew a converted Dash 8-300 testbed with one propeller driven by a hydrogen fuel cell. The company raised roughly $100 million from backers including GE Aviation, American Airlines, JetBlue Ventures, Airbus Ventures, Toyota Ventures and Mitsubishi. Unable to raise further equity or debt or to find a buyer, it ceased operations on 27 June 2024 and liquidated. It was a hardware and fuel-logistics business and never shipped a public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its domains no longer serve a site.

providers.name: e-CROSS
providers.description: e-CROSS is a cross-border e-commerce platform that lets international brands sell into Latin America. Acting as a Merchant of Record, it handles payment processing, currency exchange, logistics and fulfillment intelligence, customs and legal compliance, and storefront localization so merchants can expand into the region with a simple integration into their existing e-commerce stack. e-CROSS is a 500 Global portfolio company. Its public site runs on Wix and exposes a hosted, unauthenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) server plus an llms.txt for agentic AI access to public site content; e-CROSS does not currently publish a first-party developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK.

providers.name: Shurpa
providers.description: Shurpa was a healthcare logistics startup and a Techstars 2019 portfolio company, building a medical transportation management software platform focused on the population health and managed care space (AI-enabled coordination of non-emergency medical transportation and in-home healthcare services). The company raised roughly $220K across two seed rounds and has no visible operations today: the shurpa.com domain now returns HTTP 404 across all paths and is parked on CSC/UltraDNS nameservers, and no developer portal, documentation, API, OpenAPI, or .well-known surface could be found during enrichment. This profile is retained as an identity record for a dormant/defunct provider with no discoverable API surface.

providers.name: Delta Tucker Holdings
providers.description: Delta Tucker Holdings was the holding company for DynCorp International, a provider of specialized mission-critical professional and support services to government and commercial customers, including aviation services, logistics, and training. DynCorp's operations were acquired and integrated into Amentum in 2020. Delta Tucker Holdings does not publish public APIs; this profile is preserved as a corporate-history index.

providers.name: Noon
providers.description: Noon is a Dubai-headquartered e-commerce marketplace and digital ecosystem launched in 2017 as a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Emirati businessman Mohamed Alabbar. Frequently described as the Amazon of the MENA region, Noon operates as the leading online shopping destination across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Egypt, offering electronics, mobiles, fashion, beauty, home, appliances, baby, and grocery categories through a hybrid first-party and third-party seller marketplace. Beyond the core marketplace, Noon has expanded into a lifestyle super-app spanning Noon Food (quick-service restaurant delivery competing with Talabat and Deliveroo), Noon Daily (next-day grocery delivery), Noon Minutes (15-minute instant grocery and essentials delivery), Noon Pay and the Noon mobile wallet (QR payments, bill pay, and a co-branded credit card), Noon VIP (loyalty/subscription), NowNow (on-demand delivery in KSA), and SIVVI (acquired regional fashion brand). Noon operates its own last-mile logistics arm and warehouses across the region, and provides a Fulfilled by Partner Integration (FBPI) program with commercial APIs that allow third-party sellers and channel-integration partners (ChannelEngine, Unicommerce, Vinculum, Ecom Energize and others) to programmatically publish catalog, sync inventory, and manage shipments. These APIs are gated to onboarded sellers and certified integrators inside the noon.partners environment — there is no general public developer portal, no published OpenAPI specification, and no Noon-maintained SDKs, CLIs, or open-source repositories.

providers.name: 大易有塑 (dayi35.com)
providers.description: dayi35.com (大易有塑, Dayi Yousu) is a Chinese business-to-business e-commerce and trading platform for plastics and chemical raw materials, operated out of Dongguan, Guangdong. The platform runs an online mall covering general-purpose plastics (ABS, EVA, GPPS, HIPS, LLDPE), engineering plastics (PA6, PA66, PBT, PC, PET, PMMA, PPS, LCP), modified and recycled resins, and chemical additives such as titanium dioxide, carbon black, flame retardants and release agents. Alongside the mall it operates a buyer request-for-quote board (求购), a daily domestic and international price and market-data service, industry news, and supply-chain services spanning warehousing, logistics distribution, and e-commerce enablement for plastics and chemicals enterprises. Buyer and seller activity runs through an authenticated member console at /uc. The site is filed under Chinese ICP licence 粤ICP备15037802号.

providers.name: Lula
providers.description: Lula Technologies, Inc. was a Miami, Florida insurance-infrastructure company founded by twin brothers Matthew Vega-Sanz (CEO) and Michael Vega-Sanz (President). It started as the car-sharing startup Lula Rides and pivoted during the COVID-19 pandemic into an API-first — widely described at the time as "Stripe-like" — insurance platform for small and mid-sized car rental, car-sharing, trucking and logistics fleet operators, bundling driver vetting and risk assessment, fraud detection, driver-history checks, episodic/on-demand policy issuance and claims handling behind a single API underwritten through licensed insurance partners. It raised an $18M Series A in July 2021 and a $35.5M Series B, and its public developer surface was a Postman documenter collection alongside a developer portal at www.lula.is/developers. In 2024 Lula divested its insurance division to Nantucket Capital Corp, a San Diego MGA, headcount fell from roughly 150 to about 19, and the founders sold the company. The domain lula.is has since left the company's control — it now delegates to parkingcrew.net and serves a "This domain may be for sale!" holding page — the API host api.lula.is is gone, and the Postman collection returns 404. No public API surface remains. NOTE FOR FUTURE PASSES — the same founders later built a SEPARATE company, Gail (legal entity Nothing Technologies, Inc., meetgail.com), which does operate a live developer surface; Gail is not a rename of Lula and none of its artifacts may be attributed to this profile. Two other unrelated companies also trade as "Lula": Lula (lula.life, property maintenance) and Lula Commerce (lulacommerce.com, convenience retail). This profile is retained as a historical company record.
